title: New Lock Stoplogs
description: THIS IS A PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE. THIS IS NOT THE REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, NOR INFORMATION FOR BID. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District intends to solicit for the New Lock Stoplogs to provide fabrication services to the Soo Project Office (SPO) in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. The project involves the fabrication and delivery of two complete sets of stoplogs (16 total). The fabricator shall be certified under AISC 207-23 as an Advanced Bridge Fabricator, Intermediate Bridge Fabricator, or Advanced Hydraulic Fabricator. The fabricator shall also have a Fracture Control Endorsement (FCE). Each full set of stoplogs includes 7 standard (non-filling) stoplogs and 1 filling stoplog (incl. 2 butterfly valve assemblies). Stoplogs shall be delivered by barge or ship to the Soo Locks in Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan. The Government will off-load stoplogs from barges. Ships shall off-load stoplogs to a designated area accessible to the ship. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code is 332312 � Fabricated Structural Metal Manufacturing, which has a small business size standard of 500 employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 9520 � Structural Shapes. The Solicitation will be issued as a 100% total small business set-aside. The Government intends to issue a firm-fixed price contract. Anticipated Solicitation Posting Date: November 2026. Anticipated Bid Due Date: December 2026. The solicitation package materials, documents, drawings, specifications, and attachments to the anticipated solicitation will be available only electronically and via the PIEE Solicitation Module and/or SAM.gov which is free of charge. Hard copy documents will NOT be supplied by the Government to any interested parties as a result of this pre-solicitation notice or the upcoming solicitation. Please note the Government will not be maintaining a bidders list during the solicitation period. However, vendors are strongly encouraged to review the "Interested Vendors List" found on sam.gov for this requirement. title: P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA
description: PRE-SOLICITATION SYNOPSIS NOTICE ONLY: THE SOLICITATION WILL BE AVAILABLE ON OR ABOUT NOVEMBER 5, 2026, AT HTTPS://SAM.GOV/. THE SOLICITATION NUMBER IS N6945027R0006, FOR THE DESIGN-BID-BUILD (DBB) CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES, KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA PROJECT TITLE: DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT, FY27, P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES, KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA PSC: Y1LB - Construction of Highways, Roads, Streets, Bridges, and Railways NAICS: 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. Project Description: The project will include but is not limited to the following: Constructs railroad trackage to connect and facilitate the transfer from commercial rail to the on-base processing facility at Cape Canaveral. Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. The estimated Period of Performance is 527 calendar days. The best value continuum source selection process to be used for this acquisition is the tradeoff approach, as described in FAR 15.103-1. The best value tradeoff process is appropriate and permits evaluation of proposals based on price competition, technical merit, confidence assessment and other factors; permits impartial and comprehensive evaluation of offeror proposals; permits discussions if necessary; and ensures selection of the source whose performance provides the best value to the Government. A sources sought notice was posted to sam.gov on September 10, 2026 requesting small business industry interested and capability statement. Based on responses from the notice it was determined that the requirement should be issued as full and open. The solicitation will be a negotiated DBB acquisition. Proposals will be solicited in a two part submission for a single solicitation. The solicitation will utilize source selection procedures, which require offerors to submit a technical proposal, past performance and experience information, and a price proposal for evaluation by the Government. Award will be made to the offeror whose total price and technical proposal offer the best value to the Government. Competition Requirements: Unrestricted basis, under full and open competition. title: RFI: Fort Wolters H Barracks
description: SUBJECT: Sources Sought (RFI) � Fort Wolters H Barracks, Mineral Wells, Texas DISCLAIMER. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market intelligence, information, and planning purposes. It does not constitute a Request for Proposals (RFP), a Request for Qualifications (RFQ), or a commitment by the Government to write, issue, or award an agreement. The Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All response costs will be borne solely by the interested party. PURPOSE. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, is conducting active public market intelligence to gauge industry interest, capacity, and capability from commercial construction firms, design-builders, and Non-Traditional Defense Contractors (NDCs). The intent is to gather critical feedback regarding advanced commercial construction methodologies, project delivery risks, and acquisition preferences to support our upcoming project delivery selection. ACQUISITION STRATEGY & NON-FAR MODEL. Statutory Authority: This project will potentially be executed as a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB) project utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA) pursuant to 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Non-FAR Environment: Prospective partners are advised that the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) does NOT apply to this procurement. The negotiated, bilateral Other Transaction Agreement will serve as the sole governing contract. Standard FAR clauses are inapplicable, though federal statutory constraints (such as federal fiscal law, criminal statutes, and general civil laws) remain fully applicable. Phased Agreement Mechanics: PBD Procurement Process: Phase 1, Design & Pre-Construction Services, a design-builder will be selected through a qualifications-based selection (QBS) process. The government will then negotiate a fee for Phase 1 services. There is no requirement to submit price proposals or design concepts during the initial selection. Phase 2, Final Design & Construction, is executed via a bilateral modification to the OT Agreement upon successful negotiation of a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) at approximately 65% design maturity. The Agreement contains an "off-ramp" clause allowing the Government to retain the design and procure construction separately if GMP negotiations fail. DBtB Procurement Process: Solicitation and evaluation during Phase 1 focuses on the qualifications, past performance, and integrated Design-Build experience of each offeror. The Government is evaluating the team and not necessarily how the offeror will design the structure. The Phase 1 evaluation results in the selection of three of the most highly qualified, competitive teams to proceed to Phase 2. Phase 2, the Government will issue the final RFP exclusively to the down-selected teams. This RFP includes the validated, performance-based requirements, establishes the firm Construction Cost Limit (CCL), and clearly defines the basic scope. Note: See link to provide industry feedback https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/ZQ8Rm8MaN7

title: Upgrade Fire Detection System at FDC Honolulu, Hawaii
description: 10/21/2026 - Amendment 0005 - Incorporate revised response to bidder's question #13, update construction wage determination, and extend bid due date to November 4, 2026, no later than 2:00 pm CST. -- 10/15/2026 - Amendment 0004 - Invite bidders who submitted acceptable technical proposals in Step-One to submit a bid in Step-Two. Step-Two Bid due date is October 28, 2026, no later than 2:00 pm CST. Only American Alarm Co., Inc. and Elite Pacific Construction, Inc. are allowed to submit bids. Further bid instructions will be e-mailed to these contractors. -- 8/17/2026 - Amendment 0003 - Extend Step-One technical proposals due date to August 26, 2026, no later than 1:00 pm CST. -- 8/5/2026 - Amendment 0002 - Incorporate bidder's question with response. -- 8/3/2026 - Amendment 0001 - Incorporate pre-bid site visit meeting minutes, sign-in sheet, photo, responses to bibbers' questions, increase period of performance. Correct soliciation number on Instructions for Two-Step Sealed Bidding document. -- THIS IS A COMBINED SYNOPSIS-SOLICITATION OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) is issuing a Two-Step Invitation for Bid (IFB). The solicitation will result in one (1) firm-fixed-price contract for a project titled Upgrade Fire Detection System at the Federal Detention Center (FDC) located in Honolulu, Hawaii. FDC Honolulu is a federal correctional institution located at 351 Elliott Street, Honolulu, HI 96819. The project consists of furnishing all equipment, materials, and labor for the complete construction to upgrade the fire detection system at the FDC Honolulu. The specification and construction drawings included in the attachments of this solicitation provides the requirements for the project. Site Visit: A site visit is planned for Tuesday, July 21, 2026. The details are in solicitation attachment Instructions for Two-Step Sealed Bidding, pages 3-4. Invitation For Bid (IFB) Evaluation Criteria: This solicitation and resulting contract is using the Two-Step Sealed Bidding procurement method as described in FAR Deviation 14.211. The two-step procedure is a combination of competitive procedures designed to obtain the benefits of sealed bidding while ensuring only technically acceptable firms participate in the priced sealed bid. The process allows for the Step-One technical proposal submission and evaluation to be performed to identify firms eligible for Step-Two. Contractors participating in the solicitation will submit a technical proposal in accordance with the solicitation attachments Instructions for Two-Step Sealed Bidding and Step-One Technical Proposal Factors. Submissions will be evaluated for acceptability in accordance with solicitation attachment Step-One Technical Proposal Evaluation. Under this bidding process, Step-One consists of the request for technical proposal, evaluation, and (if necessary) discussion of a technical proposal. The submission requirements of Step One, Request for Technical Proposal, shall not include any prices or pricing information. Only one (1) technical proposal may be submitted by each offeror. The technical proposals will be evaluated for technical acceptability. A notice of �acceptable� or �unacceptable� will be forwarded to each Step-One offeror upon completion of the technical proposal evaluation and final determination. The names of the offerors that submitted acceptable technical proposals will be listed on the Government�s SAM.gov solicitation posting for the benefit of prospective subcontractors. In Step-Two, an amendment to the solicitation will be issued along with any updates to the technical specifications and construction drawings to only those bidders whose technical proposals are determined to be acceptable in Step-One. The normal sealed bidding process in FAR Part 14 will be followed in Step-Two. Only bids based upon technical proposals determined to be acceptable, either initially or as a result of discussions for Step- One, will be considered for award. Bidders must comply with the 100% completed specifications and construction drawings and the bidder�s acceptable technical proposal. Bid bonds are not required to be submitted with the Step-One technical proposal. Bid bonds will be required to be submitted with the Step-Two bid submission. Payment and Performance Bonds will be required for the full amount (100%) at the time of contract award before the Notice to Proceed (NTP) can be issued. Any secured/locked documents (Specifications and Drawings) with the solicitation will require an active vendor registration at https://SAM.gov as well as your Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) associated with your System for Award Management (SAM) registration. The controlled documents will not be emailed. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Companion 36.101-3, the estimated magnitude of the project lies between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. (NOTE: This range is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. title: DA01--VA-27-00015330 - Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC)
description: Request for Information Request for information Page 1 of 2 DESCRIPTION Request for Information Synopsis Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC) Enterprise Data Products, API Delivery, Data Access and Sharing 1.0 RFI Synopsis Narrative Background and Purpose The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information & Technology (OIT), is conducting market research to inform a planned future acquisition known as Mission-Oriented Services for Application Integration and Capabilities (MOSAIC). MOSAIC is focused on positioning VA s authoritative data as a trustworthy, well-structured enterprise asset that can be reliably consumed in whatever form the mission requires. VA seeks to continuously improve this data so that it can be relied upon as genuinely authoritative and to make that same data available through the full range of access patterns the mission requires: real-time transactional APIs, bulk and analytical access suitable for data-lake and large-scale workloads, event-driven and streaming exchange, and the governed, well-described, AI-ready data products that models, agents, and automated features increasingly require. A single data domain today may be served reliably through one interface yet remain difficult to access in another or exposed broadly while portions of its underlying content are known to be incomplete or unreliable. The VA intends for MOSAIC to close these gaps so that the same trusted data can be accessed, reused, and acted upon across many mission and technology use cases. VA is using this RFI to better understand how this mission should evolve over the next five to ten years and what technical, operating, and acquisition decisions made today would best position VA for that future. VA currently supports mission data and integration products that may form part of the initial MOSAIC baseline, including VA Profile, VADIR, HDR, existing API products, and related integration capabilities. The final inventory, transition boundaries, and allocation of work among MOSAIC, VA organizations, and other enterprise contracts have not been determined. MOSAIC will also operate in an environment that depends on enterprise data platforms, catalogs, identity services, infrastructure, security capabilities, and other agency- or vendor-managed services. VA does not want this market research to assume that today's API, integration, architecture, delivery, or operating models should simply be carried forward. VA is specifically seeking industry's perspective on how AI agents, real-time data access, event-driven architecture, interoperability standards, reusable data products, automation, and other emerging technologies may change the way VA exposes, exchanges, governs, and operates mission data. VA also wants industry to identify capabilities, architecture patterns, tools, and operating practices that should be reduced, retired, consolidated, or replaced as the ecosystem evolves. This RFI is intended to inform the MOSAIC Performance Work Statement (PWS), technical and operating model, transition approach, performance framework, commercial structure, acquisition strategy, and source-selection design. VA has not made final decisions regarding the future-state architecture, delivery model, single- versus multiple-award structure, contract type, ordering approach, period of performance, ceiling, pricing model, or final technical evaluation factors. Industry is encouraged to challenge VA's current assumptions and recommend alternatives supported by demonstrated operational, technical, and commercial experience. Areas for Industry Perspective VA is seeking forward-looking industry perspective on the following areas rather than validation of a predetermined solution: The future state VA should pursue over the next five to ten years for positioning its authoritative data as a trustworthy, well-structured, multi-modal enterprise asset, including the capabilities and architectural principles that should define that target state. How AI agents, event-driven and real-time data patterns, interoperability standards, data products, automation, and emerging technologies may change the role of traditional APIs, point-to-point integrations, middleware, and manual integration services. Which current capabilities, technical patterns, tools, and operating practices VA should plan to eliminate, consolidate, or replace over the next five years, and what should replace them. The relative advantages of a traditional managed-services model versus a platform-first operating model built around standardized, reusable capabilities, self-service, automation, common engineering patterns, and measurable product or mission outcomes. How VA should sustain mission-critical services during modernization while improving availability, recovery, resilience, observability, security, maintainability, and interoperability. How VA can scale to future enterprise demand without relying primarily on open-ended labor or team augmentation, including ways to classify complexity, size work, and introduce new in-scope capabilities consistently. How commercial and performance models should evolve as automation increases, including how VA should measure value, validate productivity and cost reductions, and avoid incentives that reward activity or consumption rather than outcomes. How VA should preserve portability, Government access to technical assets and data, and the ability to transition products and services without dependence on proprietary contractor-controlled tooling. Current Environment and Working Assumptions For purposes of responding to this RFI, respondents may assume that MOSAIC could include some combination of continuous data-quality assessment and improvement, multi-modal data access and delivery (transactional, bulk/analytical, event-driven, and AI-ready data products), data sharing and integration, sustainment and operational support, modernization, data landscape assessment and roadmap planning, and transition activities for a defined initial product set, with the potential for additional in-scope enterprise demand over time. Respondents should not assume that current architecture, tools, licenses, organizational boundaries, or delivery practices will remain unchanged. Where a recommendation depends on a particular Government-furnished platform, commercial product, licensing model, authoritative data source, or separately managed enterprise service, identify that dependency and explain why it matters. What VA Is Asking Industry to Address VA requests candid, experience-based responses focused on the future state VA should pursue, and the practical decisions required to achieve it. Responses should distinguish between current demonstrated capabilities and future roadmap capabilities and should identify material assumptions, dependencies, risks, transition considerations, and conditions necessary for success. VA seeks recommendations that will improve the quality, reliability, and reusability of its authoritative data and make that data readily consumable through multiple access modes, including AI-enabled uses. Recommendations should also address how VA can simplify the environment, increase reuse and interoperability, reduce technical debt and avoidable operating costs, and improve resilience and security. VA is particularly interested in durable enterprise capabilities rather than approaches that preserve existing structures for their own sake. This RFI is issued solely for information gathering and acquisition planning purposes and is intended to support the Department of Veterans Affairs' market research and ongoing refinement of requirements, acquisition strategy, contract scope, sequencing, and commercial structure. This RFI is not a solicitation and does not constitute an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation, award

title: Military Plans Specialist Support Services
description: 2. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION & Performance duties 2.1 Scope of Support The Contractor shall provide operational and strategic planning advisory support to the Area Support Group-Jordan (ASG-J) Operations Directorate (S-3), assisting in the coordination, development, and execution of comprehensive operational plans, contingency plans, exercises, and force protection programs in support of United States Army Central (USARCENT) and adjacent USCENTCOM entities. 2.2 Core Responsibilities and Duty Allocation The following major duties (percentages approximate effort allocation) are derived from the official Army Position Description: Physical Security and Force Protection Planning (approx. 30%): Develop, implement, review, and update comprehensive physical security and force protection plans, policies, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Assist the ASG-J Provost Marshal Office (PMO) in identifying vulnerabilities and performing technical force protection inspections, assessments, and surveys. Coordinate Mission Assurance Assessments (MAA) with USARCENT, conduct associated In-Progress Reviews (IPRs) and briefings and develop corrective action plans for identified deficiencies. Coordinate with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to conduct physical security/force protection reviews on installation master plans, construction projects, and facility renovations pursuant to applicable DoD and Army regulations. Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning / Contingency Plans (approx. 30%): Integrate deliberate and crisis action planning support across USARCENT, subordinate formations, and USCENTCOM. Serve as technical lead and project coordinator for contingency planning efforts, contributing directly to the drafting and refinement of Operations Plans (OPLANs), Concept Plans (CONPLANs), Operations Orders (OPORDs), Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs), and Functional Plans. Utilize the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) / Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) enterprise to formulate cyber operations annexes, appendices, and operational deployment workflows for deployed forces. Exercise and Training Support / MDMP-JOPP (approx. 20%): Support ASG-J S-3 operations to ensure field and command-post exercises align with USARCENT doctrine, policies, and priorities. Apply deep operational understanding of Commander�s Intent, Running Estimates, Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB), Deliberate Planning, and the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP) / Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP) across Unified, Joint, Combined, and Service-component echelons. Facilitate Operational Planning Teams (OPTs) and Joint Planning Groups (JPGs); conduct Course of Action (COA) development, analysis (wargaming), comparison, and decision briefing preparation for senior leadership. Inter-Agency Representation and Staff Coordination (approx. 20%): Represent the ASG-J S-3 during cross-functional working groups, operational syncs, and planning conferences. Liaise with internal directorates, tenant units, host-nation representatives, and higher headquarters to align ASG-J operational roadmaps with theater campaign goals. 2.3 Mandatory Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Comprehensive proficiency in Army regulations and doctrine pertaining to Base Operations Support-Integrator (BOS-I), Common-User Logistics/Base Operations (COM-I), Physical Security, and Force Protection. Working knowledge of DoD directives, relevant U.S. statutes, and bilateral frameworks, including the U.S.�Jordanian Defense Cooperation Agreement (DCA). Familiarity with USARCENT, 1st Theater Sustainment Command (1TSC), and USCENTCOM operational architecture and associated OPLANs/CONPLANs. Working knowledge of Theater Provided Equipment (TPE), Modified Table of Organization and Equipment (MTOE), and Tables of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) structures. Exceptional written and verbal military communication skills, including experience authoring formal executive summaries, military orders, and general officer-level briefings. 3. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS & CONDITIONS OF PERFORMANCE Security Clearance: Personnel assigned to this contract must possess an active, verified SECRET security clearance granted by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) prior to performance start date, with the ability to maintain eligibility throughout contract execution. Deployability & Travel: Contractor personnel must be deployable and eligible for overseas travel. Business travel (Temporary Duty - TDY) within the USCENTCOM Area of Responsibility (Jordan and adjacent Middle Eastern countries) is anticipated up to 20% of annual performance. Medical & Theater Entry Requirements: Contractor personnel must meet all CENTCOM Mod/theater-specific medical clearance standards, including required immunization profiles (e.g., seasonal influenza and applicable DoD overseas health mandates) and Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT) / Letter of Authorization (LOA) processing. DFARS Compliance Notice: Offerors are advised that any follow-on solicitation will include mandatory overseas clauses, including DFARS 252.225-7040 (Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States), SOFA/DCA compliance, and Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements.

title: Sources Sought Notice � 8(a) Small Business Capability Inquiry: Personnel Readiness Assistance Team (PRAT) Senior Personnel Analyst
description: NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center San Diego (FLCSD) is conducting market research to identify interested and capable businesses that can provide Personnel Readiness Assistance Team (PRAT) Senior Personnel Analyst support services for Commander, Naval Surface Force, U.S. Pacific Fleet (COMNAVSURFPAC). This Sources Sought Notice is issued for planning and market-research purposes only. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing or submitting a response. Any information submitted in response to this notice is voluntary and will be used solely to support acquisition planning. The Government anticipates awarding this requirement as an 8(a) set-aside using a Firm-Fixed-Price contract type, with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. This requirement has historically been awarded through the Small Business Administration�s 8(a) Business Development Program. For any resultant small business set-aside contract or task order, FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply. To be considered capable of performing this requirement, small business prime contractors must demonstrate the ability to perform at least 50 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, either independently or in conjunction with other similarly situated entities, as defined in FAR 52.219-14. Respondents proposing teaming arrangements or subcontractors shall identify the anticipated percentage of work to be subcontracted and specify whether proposed subcontractors are similarly situated small business concerns or large business concerns. COMNAVSURFPAC requires PRAT Senior Personnel Analyst support to augment its capacity to conduct Command Readiness Assessment Visits (CRAVs) and personnel readiness assist visits aboard Surface Ships. The requirement is driven by increased CRAV workload resulting from the incorporation of CRAV requirements into Home Port Change instructions and expanded CRAV training requirements for Naval Surface Groups. These requirements have increased the demand for assessment planning, travel coordination, shipboard assist visits, checklist management, report consolidation, corrective-action planning, and onsite program training. The contractor shall support the PRAT and CRAV Lead in assessing afloat administrative and personnel readiness programs, with emphasis on Drug and Alcohol Program Advisor (DAPA) and Urinalysis Program Coordinator (UPC) program compliance. The contractor shall be prepared to perform work at Naval Base 32nd Street and aboard Surface Ships during required assist visits. The anticipated effort includes continental United States and international travel to Everett, Washington; Pearl Harbor, Hawaii; Yokosuka, Japan; and Sasebo, Japan. Personnel performing international travel shall possess a valid passport. Interested parties should carefully review the Sources Sought attachment and the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for complete details regarding the required scope, performance standards, deliverables, personnel qualifications, security requirements, travel requirements, and instructions for submitting a response. The Government anticipates a Firm-Fixed-Price contract type with a 12-month base period and four 12-month option periods. This requirement is a follow-on requirement to the 8(a) sole-source contract, N00244-26-P-S035, awarded to Kiakahi, LLC. Anticipated NAICS Code: 611430 Small Business Size Standard: 15 (millions of dollars) Interested parties shall submit a capability statement of no more than five pages, excluding the completed reference information sheet. Tables, charts, organizational charts, process charts, and similar illustrations may be used but will count toward the five-page limitation. Electronic responses are preferred. Telephonic requests for information will not be honored. Respondents are responsible for appropriately marking proprietary information. The Government will not conduct capability briefings as a result of this notice. Responses that do not conform to these instructions may not be considered. Generic corporate brochures will not be reviewed. This is a sources sought for market research purposes. The Government�s requirement may change at any time. DO NOT submit proposals in response to this sources sought. This announcement is not a contract, request for proposal, a promise to contract, or a commitment of any kind on the part of the Government. The Navy will not assume liability for costs incurred by a company for capability statement preparation or marketing efforts; therefore, any cost in response to this notice is not considered an allowable direct charge to the Government. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Dionte Grays.

title: Military Plans Specialist Support Services
description: 2. REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION & Performance duties 2.1 Scope of Support The Contractor shall provide operational and strategic planning advisory support to the Area Support Group-Jordan (ASG-J) Operations Directorate (S-3), assisting in the coordination, development, and execution of comprehensive operational plans, contingency plans, exercises, and force protection programs in support of United States Army Central (USARCENT) and adjacent USCENTCOM entities. 2.2 Core Responsibilities and Duty Allocation The following major duties (percentages approximate effort allocation) are derived from the official Army Position Description: Physical Security and Force Protection Planning (approx. 30%): Develop, implement, review, and update comprehensive physical security and force protection plans, policies, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Assist the ASG-J Provost Marshal Office (PMO) in identifying vulnerabilities and performing technical force protection inspections, assessments, and surveys. Coordinate Mission Assurance Assessments (MAA) with USARCENT, conduct associated In-Progress Reviews (IPRs) and briefings and develop corrective action plans for identified deficiencies. Coordinate with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) to conduct physical security/force protection reviews on installation master plans, construction projects, and facility renovations pursuant to applicable DoD and Army regulations. Deliberate and Crisis Action Planning / Contingency Plans (approx. 30%): Integrate deliberate and crisis action planning support across USARCENT, subordinate formations, and USCENTCOM. Serve as technical lead and project coordinator for contingency planning efforts, contributing directly to the drafting and refinement of Operations Plans (OPLANs), Concept Plans (CONPLANs), Operations Orders (OPORDs), Fragmentary Orders (FRAGOs), and Functional Plans. Utilize the Joint Operation Planning and Execution System (JOPES) / Adaptive Planning and Execution (APEX) enterprise to formulate cyber operations annexes, appendices, and operational deployment workflows for deployed forces. Exercise and Training Support / MDMP-JOPP (approx. 20%): Support ASG-J S-3 operations to ensure field and command-post exercises align with USARCENT doctrine, policies, and priorities. Apply deep operational understanding of Commander�s Intent, Running Estimates, Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB), Deliberate Planning, and the Military Decision Making Process (MDMP) / Joint Operational Planning Process (JOPP) across Unified, Joint, Combined, and Service-component echelons. Facilitate Operational Planning Teams (OPTs) and Joint Planning Groups (JPGs); conduct Course of Action (COA) development, analysis (wargaming), comparison, and decision briefing preparation for senior leadership. Inter-Agency Representation and Staff Coordination (approx. 20%): Represent the ASG-J S-3 during cross-functional working groups, operational syncs, and planning conferences. Liaise with internal directorates, tenant units, host-nation representatives, and higher headquarters to align ASG-J operational roadmaps with theater campaign goals. 2.3 Mandatory Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) Comprehensive proficiency in Army regulations and doctrine pertaining to Base Operations Support-Integrator (BOS-I), Common-User Logistics/Base Operations (COM-I), Physical Security, and Force Protection. Working knowledge of DoD directives, relevant U.S. statutes, and bilateral frameworks, including the U.S.�Jordanian Defense Cooperation Agreement (DCA). Familiarity with USARCENT, 1st Theater Sustainment Command (1TSC), and USCENTCOM operational architecture and associated OPLANs/CONPLANs. Working knowledge of Theater Provided Equipment (TPE), Modified Table of Organization and Equipment (MTOE), and Tables of Distribution and Allowances (TDA) structures. Exceptional written and verbal military communication skills, including experience authoring formal executive summaries, military orders, and general officer-level briefings. 3. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS & CONDITIONS OF PERFORMANCE Security Clearance: Personnel assigned to this contract must possess an active, verified SECRET security clearance granted by the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) prior to performance start date, with the ability to maintain eligibility throughout contract execution. Deployability & Travel: Contractor personnel must be deployable and eligible for overseas travel. Business travel (Temporary Duty - TDY) within the USCENTCOM Area of Responsibility (Jordan and adjacent Middle Eastern countries) is anticipated up to 20% of annual performance. Medical & Theater Entry Requirements: Contractor personnel must meet all CENTCOM Mod/theater-specific medical clearance standards, including required immunization profiles (e.g., seasonal influenza and applicable DoD overseas health mandates) and Synchronized Predeployment and Operational Tracker (SPOT) / Letter of Authorization (LOA) processing. DFARS Compliance Notice: Offerors are advised that any follow-on solicitation will include mandatory overseas clauses, including DFARS 252.225-7040 (Contractor Personnel Supporting U.S. Armed Forces Deployed Outside the United States), SOFA/DCA compliance, and Defense Base Act (DBA) insurance requirements.

title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for Electronic Fish Barriers
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Chicago District, is issuing this sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirement of six high voltage power supplies (HVPS) for Barriers IIA and IIB near Romeoville, Illinois. The intention is to procure this requirement on a competitive basis.*************BASED ON THE RESPONSES TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE/MARKET RESEARCH, THIS REQUIREMENT MAY BE SET-ASIDE FOR SMALL BUSINESSES (IN FULL OR IN PART) OR PROCURED THROUGH FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION, and multiple awards MAY be made. USACE is conducting market research to determine whether a small business set-aside is achievable under the newly restructured terms, or whether it will proceed under full and open competition with subcontracting opportunities. We recently solicited unrestricted but had a bid bust, so are restructuring our requirement with the elimination of storage requirements. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions.*************DISCLAIMER*************THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP) TO BE SUBMITTED. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. RESPPONSES WILL NOT BE RETURNED TO THE RESPONDER. NOT RESPONDING TO THIS NOTICE DOES NOT PRECLUDE PARTICIPATION IN ANY FUTURE REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB) OR RFP, IF ANY ISSUED. IF A SOLICITATION IS RELEASED, IT WILL BE SYNOPSIZED ON THE GOVERNMENT-WIDE POINT OF ENTRY (GPE). IT IS THE RESPONSIBILITY OF POTENTIAL OFFERORS TO MONITOR THE GPE FOR ADDITIONAL INFORMMATION PERTAINING TO THIS REQUIREMENT.*************PROGRAM BACKGROUND: The HPVS support Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal Electric Dispersal Barrier System, barriers IIA and IIB. These Electric Dispersal Barriers protect the Great Lakes from the invasive species.*************REQUIRED CAPABILITIES*************The Contractor shall provide engineering and site verification; design submittals; fabrication; factory acceptance testing (FAT); operator and maintenance training during or immediately after FAT; technical documentation; packaging, transportation, delivery and unloading; and warranty coverage services in support of the areas specified in Program Background (above). Further details: a) Four 1.5 megawatt (MW) high voltage power supplies for Pulser 1 and Pulser 2 at Barriers IIA and IIB. and b) Two 350 kilowatt (kW) high voltage power supplies for Pulser 3 at Barriers IIA and IIB.*************Technical capability overview*************The replacement equipment will support existing pulse generating units and capacitor banks serving the electric dispersal barriers. The following summarizes the anticipated requirement for market research; it is not a complete fabrication specification.*************Input power: 480 volts AC, three-phase, 60 hertz.*************Output ratings: each 1.5 MW unit to provide 2,000 volts DC at 750 amperes and 2,200 volts DC at approximately 682 amperes, subject to its 1.5 MW continuous power limit. Each 350 kW unit to provide up to 1,000 volts DC at 350 amperes.*************Power conversion: copper-wound transformers and a 24-pulse silicon controlled rectifier (SCR) configuration, or an equivalent approach for Government consideration that achieves the required performance and harmonic reduction.*************Integration: compatibility with existing equipment spaces, access routes, electrical connections, cooling systems, and the Pulse Generating Control System. Identify any necessary changes to existing equipment or interfaces rather than assuming they are included in this procurement.*************Controls and safety: local and remote monitoring, communications, alarms, protective devices, and interlocks compatible with facility requirements. Existing interfaces include DeviceNet; the draft SOW also addresses Modbus TCP/IP.*************Operating conditions: continuous barrier service, compatibility with the pulsed load and existing capacitor banks, and the draft SOW ambient range of 0 to 50 degrees Celsius and up to 95 percent non-condensing relative humidity.*************Cooling and handling: demonstrate feasible heat rejection within available site cooling capacity and identify equipment dimensions, weights, lifting provisions, shipping configuration, and delivery/unloading needs. Early design submittals would establish dimensions, weights, anchorage, power and control connections, communications, cooling requirements, and heat loads in sufficient detail for USACE to develop the separate installation design while fabrication proceeds. Final deliverables would include drawings of the equipment as fabricated, Operation and Maintenance manuals, test reports, training materials, and storage/preservation instructions.***************************************If your organization has the potential capacity to perform this requirement, please provide the following information*************1) Organization name, address, email address, UEI and cage code, Web site address, telephone number, and size and type of ownership for the organization, and *************2) Tailored capability statements addressing the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability. If significant subcontracting or teaming is anticipated in order to deliver technical capability, organizations should address the administrative and management structure of such arrangements. Submit concise responses in the same organized format as below. Identify assumptions and distinguish firm capabilities from proposed alternatives. Partial responses from manufacturers or prospective subcontractors are welcome; clearly identify which portions your firm can support.**************************I. Interest and role Would your firm pursue this revised requirement as a prime contractor, manufacturer supplying a prime, distributor/integrator, or team member? Identify the intended manufacturer and major work allocations, if known. Explain any barriers to submitting an offer, including whether your response depends on finding a teaming partner.*************II. Relevant capability Provide up to three examples of comparable industrial HVPS or rectifier projects, including power/voltage ratings, application, approximate completion date, and your role. Describe experience with pulsed loads, copper-wound transformers, harmonic reduction, controls integration, and liquid cooling. *************III. Technical feasibility Identify requirements that would prevent participation, materially increase cost or lead time, or require an exception. Address the 24-pulse approach or proposed equivalent, output ratings, ambient conditions, cooling capacity and water quality, controls/protocol compatibility, physical fit, and any facility modifications. Describe the specific clarification or performance-based alternative recommended.*************Factory testing and training Describe available test facilities and a practical FAT approach for both ratings. Manufacturing and FAT would occur at the contractor/manufacturer facility. Distinguish full-power tests from separate full-voltage/full-current tests or simulations, and identify limitations in reproducing the installed pulsed load. Recommend measurable acceptance criteria and the equipment or site data needed. Confirm ability to train Government personnel during or immediately after FAT.*************IV. description: **W912EE** Arkabutla Lake Water Plant Rehab and Pre-fabricated Metal Building Installation This is a solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO Part 12, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. Solicitation Number W912EE27QA002 is being issued as a request for quote (RFQ) with the intent to issue one Firm-Fixed Price Contract. This solicitation is being issued under 100% small business set aside. The NAICS code for this procurement is 332311, Prefabricated Metal Building and Component Manufacturing, with a size standard of 750 employees. This procurement is being conducted in accordance with regulations at RFO Part 12 - Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Arkabutla lake Project, has a requirement to procure one metal building to cover and protect the new well. Arkabutla Lake Project has previously had a new well installed and now requires the old well to be abandoned and the surrounding small 30 x 50 building to be rehabbed to continue to protect the new well. The USACE personnel will perform prep work prior to deliver and install by removing the old building where replacement pre-fabricated building will be delivered and installed. Please see below for details. General Specification: Abandon old well Install new plumbing includes valves to meet AWWA C-509 specs, flange fitting to meet AWWA specs, watts 2� pressure reducer, 2� flange master meter, Stenner model 45MHP10 chemical pump, 3 phase air compressor, accessories and fittings to connect and create a working system Purchase, deliver, & install one (1) 30�x50� pre-fabricated metal Red Iron open span building with 12� tall eaves, 26-gauge roof & walls, one (1) roll up door, one (1) 3�x7� walk through door, insulation, and gutters. Building will include engineer�s stamped drawings for the building and a set of anchor bolt plans. Sand blast and paint tank with one (1) coat Tnemec-Zinc 3-5ml inside and out. Second coat inside Tnemec series 21 6-9ml. Third coat inside Tnemec series 216-9ml. Second coat outside L140 epoxy 6-9ml. Third coat outside 1094 urethane 5-7ml. Install new electrical including 200-amp enclosed circuit breaker outside (2020 NEC requirement), 200-amp main breaker panel inside, pump control panel with motor starter to control well, disconnect at well, six (6) 8� long LED strip lights, two (2) 55 watt outside lights with photocell, ten (10) 120V outlets including an outside GFCI, 3 phase circuit for air compressor, and reconnect existing pressure controls on tank The contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, tools, equipment, and tools necessary for purchase and installation no later than 120 days after award. Additional information about the specifications for this equipment is listed in the scope of work. All Offerors shall submit a quote with content as specified herein. Quotes submitted without the specified content may be determined unsuccessful and removed from further consideration. Offers are encouraged to review all clauses that are incorporated into this solicitation. ****SPECIAL ATTENTION SHOULD BE FOCUSED ON RFO 52.212-2 EVALUATION � COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS, AS THIS CLAUSE OUTLINES THE EVALUATION FACTORS AND BASIS FOR AWARD FOR THIS REQUIREMENT. **** The government intends to make one award for one firm fixed price contract. Offers for less than the required delivery will not be accepted. The Government intends to award without discussions while reserving the right to hold discussions if determined advantageous to the Government. Offerors are encouraged to provide their best proposed pricing in their initial offer. Notes to Offerors: A BIDDING SCHEDULE MUST BE SENT IN WITH YOUR QUOTE. Quotes shall be submitted electronically via email, to: afton.riles@usace.army.mil. For questions and technical inquiries please see instructions below. You are responsible for reading all information contained in this solicitation and all attachments if any posted with it. title: WY BR WYAO US20(1) US 20 and Hayden Arch Bridge Repairs
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR BID � PLANS AND SPECIFICATIONS ARE NOT AVAILABLE. THIS NOTICE IS BEING ISSUED TO DETERMINE IF THERE IS SUFFICIENT INTEREST FROM QUALIFIED PRIME CONTRACTORS who are small businesses, HUBZone small businesses, woman owned small business concerns, 8(a) small businesses, or service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses and who intend to submit a bid for this solicitation to allow for a set-aside in one of these programs. Interested businesses must submit the following by e-mail to CFLContracts@dot.gov (Attn: Laura Slauter) for receipt by close of business (2 p.m. local Denver time) on November 04, 2026. (1) A positive statement of your intention to submit a bid for this solicitation as a Prime Contractor; (2) A list of all confirmed socioeconomic categories (i.e., 8(a), small-disadvantaged business, HUBZone small business, service-disabled veteran-owned small business, EDWOSB, or WOSB status) that apply to your business; (3) A letter from a bonding agent stating your firm�s capability to bond for a single project of $5 million, and your firm�s aggregate bonding capacity; and (4) Provide a list of road construction projects of equal or greater value and scope to the WY BR WYAO US20(1) US 20 and Hayden Arch Bridge Repairs project in which you performed reconstruction of the bridge approaches, minor drainage improvements, signing, and guardrail replacement. Bridge repairs include concrete spall, crack, delamination, and patch repairs in the bridge superstructure and deck. Installing a waterproofing membrane on the bridge deck and constructing a temporary debris shield underneath the bridge. DO NOT SEND INFORMATION ON PROJECTS THAT DO NOT INCLUDE THE ABOVE WORK. The size of a small business firm includes all parents, subsidiaries, affiliates, etc. Refer to the Code of Federal Regulations 13 CFR 121.103 for information on how the SBA determines affiliation and 13 CFR 121.108 regarding the penalties for misrepresentation of size status. All firms should be certified in the System for Award Management (SAM) located at https://www.sam.gov/ PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Hayden Arch Bridge is located on Hayden Arch Road approximately 5 miles west of Cody, WY. The bridge spans the Shoshone River at approximately 5,060 feet above sea level and provides access for the Bureau of Reclamation (BOR) to the Buffalo Bill Dam Power Plant. The PS&E includes one (1) base schedule with no options. The scope also includes installing a waterproofing membrane on the bridge deck and constructing a temporary debris shield underneath the bridge. The bridge will be closed to public traffic for the duration of construction. title: Request for Information for On-Site Fabrication and Assembly of a Three-Bay High-Performance Magazine (HPM) Structure
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY AND YOUR RESPONSE IS NOT AN OFFER. SERIOUS INQUIRIES ONLY AND SUBMISSIONS MUST BE FROM A US-BASED CONTRACTOR. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTES (RFQ). NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION DOES NOT COMMIT THE GOVERNMENT TO PAY ANY COSTS INCURRED IN PREPARATION OF ANY SUBMISSION TO THIS NOTICE, OR TO CONTRACT FOR ITEMS/SERVICES. This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI marked Proprietary will be handled accordingly. Responses to the RFI will not be returned. Information provided in response to this RFI will be used to assess tradeoffs and alternatives available for determining how to proceed in the acquisition process for a solution. In accordance with RFO 15.101(c)(2), responses to this RFI are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is conducting market research to determine sources� competencies and capabilities to execute the on-site fabrication and final assembly of a three-bay, monolithic reinforced concrete High-Performance Magazine (HPM) structure. This is for a test structure for experimental purposes only and in the course of testing the structure will be completely destroyed and the site will be retrograded. The scope requires the full, in-situ assembly of the HPM structure at a designated Government test range at Fort Polk, LA. The process involves mobilizing all materials and equipment to the site, erecting temporary formwork systems, installing reinforcing steel cages, and placing concrete to form the final test structure according to the attached Description of Requirement (DOR). This is not a pre-cast or modular system; the final deliverable is the fully assembled and cured structure fabricated at its final location. The primary materials to be procured and processes to be performed are listed below. Reinforcing Steel (Rebar): Procure, deliver, and install prefabricated steel reinforcement into a intergrated cage within the formwork Cast-in-Place Concrete: Procure and received ready-mix concrete; place material into the erected formwork; perform consolidation, finishing and curing. Structural Sand Fill: Procure, deliver, and install sand into desiginated wall cavities post-concrete. Concrete Formwork: Fabricate or procure formwork panels; perform on-site erection, bracing, and subsequent stripping of the complete system for walls, slabs, and doors. Reinforced Concrete Doors: Perform on-site formwork erection, rebar installation, and concrete placement for three separate door components. Embedded Items: Procure and install all required embeds, sleeves, and plates within the formwork prior to concrete placement. A DRAFT Description of Requirement (DOR), which includes a detailed description of the structure, is attached. Please note this is subject to change. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to obtain information on the availability and capability of vendors to procure the necessary raw materials, provide shipping of materials and equipment to Fort Polk, LA, and perform the complete on-site fabrication and assembly of the structure to specification. Additionally, this RFI seeks to determine industry interest in participation for market research purposes before a Request for Quote (RFQ) is released for these requirements. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFQ or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the SAM.gov website. It is the responsibility of the potential offerors to monitor this site for additional information pertaining to this requirement. Respondents are requested to review the attached DRAFT DOR and submit responses to the following questions: 1. Contact information: Interested organizations should respond by providing the Government the following information: Company name, Address, Point of Contact, business title, Telephone number, Email address, Company Cage Code, Primary NAICS, Business Size, i.e., Large, Small (if small, state your category). Current Registration in SAM, Webpage address. 2. Capabilities Statement: A description of capabilities in providing 1) the minimum required items and capabilities described in the RFI and Draft DOR to the specified location(s) and 2) Experience. Previous procurement information, including contract numbers and customers, is recommended. 3. Business Status (based on NAICS 238120): Please indicate the business status of your company (Socio-Economic Factors: 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Business, Small Disadvantaged Business etc.). 4. Answer the following Questions: All interested contractors are requested to provide comprehensive written responses to the questions below. Question #1- Project Experience: Provide at least two (2) and no more than four (4) examples of projects completed by your company within the last 7 years that are of a similar scale and complexity to the HPM structure. For each project, provide the following details: Project Name and a brief description. Final concrete compressive strength(s) and total cubic yards placed. Approximate final reinforcing steel density (lbs/CY). A summary of your company's role (e.g., Prime Contractor, Concrete Subcontractor). Question #2- Self-Consolidating Concrete (SCC) Experience: The requirement is for 10,000 PSI SCC. Describe your company's experience with high-strength SCC. Specify your approach to: Mix design submittal and verification. Managing the high fluid pressure of SCC on formwork systems. On-site Quality Control testing Question #3- Formwork Systems: This project requires a robust, engineered formwork system. Does your company have in-house engineering capability to design and develop formwork plans, or is this service subcontracted? Please describe a challenging formwork scenario your company has successfully managed on a past project. Question #4- Reinforcing Steel: The project specifications require continuous, non-spliced rebar in many areas. Describe your company's experience and methods for installing long, heavy, and continuous reinforcing steel in congested, multi-layered wall and slab assemblies. Question #5- Core Competencies (Self-Perform vs. Subcontract): Please indicate which of the following core activities your company typically self-performs versus subcontracts: Heavy Concrete Formwork Design and Erection Reinforcing Steel Installation Concrete Placement and Finishing Earthwork and Site Logistics Materials QC Testing Question #6- Overall Capability: After reviewing the Description of Requirement, does your company have the capability to procure all materials and fully execute the on-site fabrication and assembly of the HPM structure as specified? If not, please specify which items or processes cannot be provided and why. Interested vendors must provide the above information no later than 3:00 PM Central Standard Time (CST) on 04 November 2026. Responses must be emailed to Shinita Jordan at Shinita.M.Jordan@usace.army.mil AND Sonia Boyd at Sonia.J.Boyd@usace.army.mil. Any questions related to this notice must be submitted in writing to Shinita Jordan and Sonia Boyd. Verbal questions will NOT be accepted. The Government will not reimburse companies for any costs associated with the submissions of their responses.

title: Commercial Solution Opportunity - Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) CONUS
description: Amendment #1. The following amendment extends the deadline date to November 4, 2026 4 p.m EST. The parent CSO with instructions is located at Related ID HQCAAA2701. This is a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) issued under the authority of DFARS 212.70. The Defense Commissary Agency (DeCA) is focused on modernizing business operations by actively seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and services that will enhance our ability to deliver the military pay benefit at a significant patron savings. Authorized under DFARS Subpart 212-70, this CSO enables DeCA to competitively procure solutions through a streamlined acquisition process, allowing for rapid decisions. This approach underscores our mission to expedite the award and delivery of critical technologies, products, and services, ensuring that DeCA can leverage advancements in the grocery resale industry swiftly and efficiently. By prioritizing speed in our contracting efforts, we aim to support the timely integration of cutting-edge technologies, products, and services that enhance our ability to: improve the commissary benefit; decrease costs without diminishing the benefit; improve processes that have a high risk of potential fraud, waste, or abuse; and reduce waste and decrease variation in processes. Contracts awarded under this authority will be structured as fixed-price contracts. Through this initiative, DeCA reaffirms its commitment to fostering innovation and enhancing business operations, ultimately delivering a vital benefit of the military compensation package that improves quality of life and readiness by providing grocery items at significant savings.

description: Notification of Sole Source Procurement. The Government intends to limit sources to the A/E firm URS-SmithGroup Joint Venture for additional Construction Phase Services (CPS) for the VA Louisville Medical Center project to be completed in Louisville, KY. IDIQ Contractors will be offered the opportunity to submit proposals for general construction and design-build Task Orders under this Contract as described elsewhere in this Statement of Work (SOW) and applicable Contract documents. The Contractor shall provide professional services for the planning, design, and construction necessary to meet the requirements of the individual Task Orders. Specific requirements of individual Task Orders will be issued by Request For Proposals on a Task Order basis. Task Order services shall be provided according to the general requirements described herein, and as further described in the Task Order Request For Proposals and accompanying documents. Disciplines and expertise that may be required to accomplish the scopes of the Task Orders include, but are not limited to: architecture, engineering (Disciplines: mechanical, electrical, plumbing, civil, structural and fire protection), vertical transportation, life safety, code compliance, security, historic preservation, estimating, construction project management and building construction services. 2.2 Place of Performance The Zones 1, Zone 2, Zone 3 and Zone 4 are detailed below by counties. title: Germany – Fire-alarm system installation work – Modernisierung GS Dorschbergschule - Gefahrenmelde- und Alarmanlage
description: Die Grundschule Dorschberg in Wörth a. Rh. wurde 1966 baulich errichtet und liegt hinter dem Mittelbau der Carl–Benz–Gesamtschule in Wörth am Rhein. Die Grundschule besteht aus vier Gebäudeteilen, zu welchen ein ein- bzw. zweigeschossiger Gebäudeteil mit Verbindungsgängen gehört sowie eine Pausenhalle mit einem Verwaltungstrakt und einem eingeschossigen Pavillonbau mit vier Pavillongebäuden. Die Gebäude sind mit Pausengängen verbunden und verfügen über zwei Toilettengebäude. Die ein- bis zweigeschossigen Gebäude wurden in massiver Bauweise mit Beton-Fertigteilen errichtet und weisen Flachdächer in unterschiedlichen Höhenlagen mit umlaufender Attika auf und wurden bis heute mehrfach saniert und modernisiert. Mitte der 1990er Jahre fand eine Betonsanierung statt. In diesem Zuge wurde ein Wärmedämm-Verbundsystem und die Alucobond-Verkleidungen der Attiken und der Fertigteilstützen angebracht. Wesentliche bauliche Maßnahmen - Der bestehende eingeschossige Klassentrakt wird aufgestockt und der bisherige Innenhofbereich zwischen den beiden bestehenden Klassentrakten wird geschlossen und überdacht. Hierzu wird die nicht ausreichend tragfähige Spannbetondecke über dem nördlichen Klassentakt zurück gebaut und durch eine neue Stahlbeton-Massivdecke ersetzt. - Das neue Obergeschoss wird in vorgefertigter Holzbauweise mit tragenden Wänden als Massivholzkonstruktion bzw. Holzständerkonstruktion und oberster Geschossdecke als Brettsperrholzkonstruktion errichtet. - Die zentrale Aula wird mit einer Glasdachkonstruktion versehen. - Die Spannbetondecke im Flurbereich über dem bestehenden Kriechkeller des Nordtraktes muss durch Stahlträger ertüchtigt werden. - Kleinteilige Grundrissänderungen im Bestand - Die Pavillons werden entkernt und zur erweiterten überdachten Pausenhoffläche - Verbesserung des Wärmeschutzes sämtlicher Gebäudehüllflächen (Dachflächen, Fenster, hinterlüftete Holzfassaden, Kellerdeckendämmung) - Modernisierung der technischen Gebäudeausrüstung inkl. kontrollierten Lüftungseinrichtung mit Wärmerückgewinnung, energiesparender Beleuchtungssysteme, Gebäudeautomation, einschließlich der digitalen Anforderungen an Schulgebäude - Optimierung des Brandschutzes und Umsetzung des schulischen Schutzkonzepts

title: Bulgaria – Dam construction work – Увеличаване на обема на долния изравнител на ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ с изграждане на язовир „Яденица“ и реверсивен напорен тунел за връзка с язовир „Чаира“, реф. № 26ИП-Р19А101
description: Предметът на обществената поръчка включва изпълнение на строително-монтажни работи и изготвяне на екзекутивна документация за обект: „Увеличаване на обема на долния изравнител на ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ с изграждане на язовир „Яденица“ и реверсивен напорен тунел за връзка с язовир „Чаира“. Основни подобекти на проекта са: • Язовирна стена и прилежащи съоръжения в т. ч. Инжекционна галерия; Шахтов преливник с отводяща галерия, бързоток и енергогасител; Основен изпускател; Контролно измервателна система; Малка ВЕЦ на екологични води; Насип за укрепване на брега на язовирното езеро в зоната на Яденишки разлом; Укрепване на свлачище в района на временния взривен склад на площадка „Яденица“; Противоерозионна защита на ската над енергогасителя на язовирната стена до пътя за връзка с короната на стената; Противоерозионна защита на изкопни откоси на експлоатационен път по левия бряг на р. Яденица, участък от km 4+860 до km 5+770; Корекция на р. Яденица след язовирната стена; Присъединяване на постоянните съоръжения (потребители) към районна мрежа 20 kV в периода на експлоатация и резервни захранвания; • Реверсивен напорен тунел и прилежащи съоръжения с подобекти: Реверсивен напорен тунел; Входно съоръжение „Яденица“; Савачна шахта „Яденица“, Савачна шахта „Чаира“; Системи за пълнене и изпразване на тунела с апаратна камера и тунела за достъп до апаратна камера; Прозорец за достъп до реверсивен напорен тунел; Изместване на водопровод за ПАВЕЦ „Чаира“ от Манавско дере; • Експлоатационни пътища; • Обслужваща сграда; Система за физическа защита. Изпълнението на поръчката ще се извърши съгласно изготвен и одобрен от Възложителя и от Министерство на регионалното развитие и благоустройство работен проект, техническата спецификация, вкл. допълнителни технически изисквания на Възложителя за поръчката. Работният проект за изпълнението на обекта, с допълнителни указания относно ценообразуването и техническите изисквания ще бъдат предоставени с поканата за участие на допуснатите кандидати - за изготвяне на оферта.

title: Sweden – Operation of a sewage plant – Hyresupphandling av pilotanläggning för vattenåtervinning
description: Kalmar Vatten AB (KVAB) bjuder in leverantörer att delta i en spännande och framtidsinriktad upphandling med fokus på att utveckla nya lösningar för en trygg och hållbar dricksvattenförsörjning. Mot bakgrund av framtida utmaningar med minskad tillgång till råvatten avser KVAB att hyra en pilotanläggning för avancerad vattenrening under en period om två år. Anläggningen ska placeras vid det nybyggda Kalmarsundsverket i Kalmar och användas för att undersöka möjligheterna att återvinna renat avloppsvatten till dricksvattenkvalitet. Pilotanläggningen ska omfatta flera avancerade reningssteg, såsom ozonering, omvänd osmos m.fl. Projektet genomförs med stöd av Tillväxtverket och Region Kalmar län.

title: F--Post-Flood Cleanup and Disaster AbatementSand Is
description: Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (Commercial Item) FAR References: FAR Part 12; FAR 5.203; FAR 19.502-2 (Total Small Business Set-Aside) NAICS Code: 562910 - Remediation Services Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Product Service Code: F108 - Environmental Systems Protection - Environmental Remediation Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Unit Price Description of Requirement The Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Canyon Country District, has an immediate abatement need for post-flood cleanup and disaster abatement at the Sand Island Ranger Station, located in a remote area approximately 4 miles west of Bluff, Utah. Flooding resulted from the San Juan River overtopping its banks and affected the following structures: * Boat House (~1,800 SF open warehouse) * Visitor Contact Center (~700 SF office/exhibition space - straw bale construction) * Law Enforcement Office (~400 SF office and sleeping area) * Residential Unit (~1,800 SF manufactured home - work primarily limited to the crawl space) The work includes hazard assessment, moisture mapping and documentation, standing water removal and drying, muck removal (excluding the residential unit), of saturated flooring/baseboards and drywall where appropriate, HEPA air scrubbing, and proper disposal of debris. A detailed Statement of Work is added to the solicitation. Only vendors capable of mobilizing quickly to a remote location in southeastern Utah and performing the required abatement work should compete for award. This is an urgent requirement. Work is expected to begin as soon as possible following award. Period of performance is 30 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. Site Visit A site visit is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026 at 11:00 MT. Interested firms are strongly encouraged to attend. Meeting Location: Campground, Sand Island Rd, Bluff, UT 84512 Sand Island Ranger Station parking area (upper lot). The Government representative will be available in the parking area. Health Advisory: The San Juan County Health Department detected E. coli in the flood waters at 25 times the typical level. Vendors should take all appropriate precautions. Vendors attending the site visit must bring all necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate for flood-damaged structures and potentially contaminated environments. Site Visit Point of Contact: Stanley Johnson Email: sjjohnson@blm.gov Phone: 435-459-2666 SAM.gov Registration All vendors must be registered and active in SAM.gov at the time of quote submission. Quotes from vendors not registered in SAM.gov will not be considered. Quote Requirements Quotes shall be prepared with firm-fixed unit prices and include the following: * Mobilization / demobilization costs (lump sum) * Labor categories and labor rates * Equipment descriptions, quantities and fixed unit rates * Hauling/removal of debris * Any other incidental costs for materials, travel, lodging, etc. Evaluation and Award Method Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. To be considered technically acceptable, an offeror must demonstrate a proven technical approach and provide evidence of prior capability to perform abatement work of this type. Among technically acceptable offers, the award will be made to the offeror with the lowest total price. Submission Instructions All quotes shall be emailed to Mark Renforth at mark_renforth@ios.doi.gov. Quotes are due no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Point of Contact (Contracting) Mark Renforth Email: mark_renforth@ios.doi.gov Phone: 801-908-5005 This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued as a total small business set-aside under NAICS 562910. All responsible small business concerns may submit a quote; timely quotes will be considered. This notice does not commit the Government to award a contract.

The FAA intends to award a single purchase order for Marathon Power equipment listed below: Line Description Quantity 00001 Period 1 (12 months) 600 00002 Shipping 600 00003 Period 2 (12 months) 600 00004 Shipping 600 00005 Period 3 (12 months) 600 00006 Shipping 600 00007 Period 4 (12 months) 600 00008 Shipping 600 00009 Period 5 (12 months) 600 00010 Shipping 600 Marathon Power is the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) of the required equipment and is the only manufacturer providing Miniature Uninterruptible Power Supply (mUPS) Supply Kits, Part number: UP-SDRU-0500-H1-KIT, in support of AJM-5 Telecommunications Integrated Services (TIS). The proposed principle North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 221122 - Electric Power Distribution, with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,100. All responses to this announcement should be addressed via email to the Contracting Officer, Tamara Maxwell, no later than 4:00 P.M. (CST), Wednesday, November 04, 2026. Subject line of email response should be titled �6973GH-26-R-00177 - MINIATURE UPS KITS � SIR�. Contact info: Contracting Officer: Tamara Maxwell tamara.m.maxwell@faa.gov 6973GH-26-R-00177-CBP MINI UPS CONTRACT - Q & A QUESTIONANSWER 1 Could you please confirm whether the intended model is UP-SDRU-0500-H1-KIT or UP-SDRS-0500-H1-KIT?The requirement UP-SDRU-0500-H1-KIT is correct. This is for a specific scenario and that runtime is required to meet ICAO standards for this equipment. 2 Page 1 of the Statement of Work (SOW) permits equivalent mUPS systems, subject to FAA Program Office approval. Could the FAA clarify whether proposed equivalent systems must receive FAA approval prior to proposal submission, or whether offerors may submit technical documentation demonstrating equivalency with their proposals for FAA review and approval during the evaluation process, prior to contract award? You may submit technical documentation demonstrating equivalency with proposal but that does not guarantee approval during evaluation or before award. 3 The SOW specifies that the 1 kVA online UPS must provide a runtime exceeding four (4) hours. Achieving this extended runtime may require a substantial external battery bank and may not be feasible within a standard configuration.Could the FAA please confirm whether this requirement is correct or was included in error? If it was included in error, will the FAA issue an amendment to correct the specification? We understand this is substantial. For most UPS vendors this will involve a large external battery connection. It also is not requiring a capacitor for this CLIN, as that would not be feasible. 4 Capacity: Is the requirement specifically for the 850VA/500W reference kit, or must proposed equipment also meet the 1kVA and 3kVA configurations listed in the SOW? If this is about watts for a fixed time, that is only for the 850. 5 Power storage: Must all proposed units use supercapacitors, or are battery-based alternatives acceptable? Only units that specifically mention capacitors need capacitors. 6 Mounting: Is DIN-rail mounting mandatory for all proposed equivalents? Only the 850 needs din rail mounting. 7 UL certification: Is UL listing or another specific safety certification required? UL listing is required. 8 Technical documentation: Are additional drawings, performance specifications, or other technical details available for manufacturers proposing an equivalent product? No further documentation can be disclosed at this time.
