title: RELIABILITY AND MAINTAINABILITY (R&M) ENGINEERING SUPPORT FOR HELICOPTER
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) RELIABILITY AND MAINTAINABILITY (R&M) ENGINEERING SUPPORT FOR HELICOPTER DIVISION WEAPON SYSTEMS Below is the general information and instructions, however the full RFI document is attached. This effort is for an 8a setaside. However, responses from disadvantaged small businesses not certified as 8a participants are encouraged to respond and will be considered on a case by case basis in accordance with current FAR regulations. Requirements The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the facilities, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to complete R&M related tasks for helicopter platforms TH-1H, UH-1N, HH-60W and MH-139. These services include, but are not limited to, conducting root cause analysis of in-service failures, developing and updating preventative maintenance procedures, recommending design modifications to improve reliability, and providing on-site technical assistance to maintenance crews, etc. Government furnished equipment will be provided as outlined in individual task orders as necessary. The Contractor is responsible for providing, maintaining, and calibrating all support equipment required at their facility or a subcontractor�s facility. Contractor furnished material or parts used for replacement shall equal or exceed the quality of the original material or parts. Contractors/Institutions responding to this market research are placed on notice that participation in this survey may not ensure participation in future solicitations or contract awards. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this survey. INSTRUCTIONS: This effort is for an 8a setaside. However, responses from disadvantaged small businesses not certified as 8a participants are encouraged to respond and will be considered on a case by case basis in accordance with current FAR regulations. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to the Program Manager (PM), Contract Specialist (CS), and Contracting Officer (CO). PURPOSE/DESCRIPTION The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the facilities, expertise, capabilities, and experience to meet qualification requirements to complete R&M related tasks for helicopter platforms TH-1H, UH-1N, HH-60W and MH-139. This requirement is for engineering support services. Our strategy is a for five to ten-year cost plus fixed-fee contract (basic plus four to nine option years) and will potentially continue through FY37. Contractor�s facility must be located in the local area of Robins Air Force Base due to the need for frequent face to face reviews and collaborative efforts. The local facility must at a minimum accommodate the program management and technical writer personnel. Manufacturing and engineering labs can be located elsewhere if necessary. When tasked by the Government, the Contractor shall perform analyses and/or services which include but are not limited to engineering research, rapid solutions, prototypes, integration and technical support services required to isolate and analyze system deficiencies, identification of appropriate solutions and production of all engineering data required to implement the improvements to prevent an adverse impact to rotary-wing aircraft reliability and maintainability. The tasking will be submitted via an Engineering Support Task Request (ESTR) form. Examples of tasks that will be required on this contract include, but are not limited to: Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) and Age Exploration (AE) program sustainment tasks such as maintenance data trend analysis, failure mode and effects analysis updates, preventative maintenance package task updates, AE candidate follow-up and updating existing RCM databases Targeted Analyses which would include failure analysis, follow- up analysis, and independent technical reviews The contractor shall provide engineering and technical expertise in support of avionics systems, aircraft structures, mechanical systems and support equipment as it applies to reliability and maintainability Development of technical procedures and technical data updates Supportability analyses Conduct research related to supportability improvement conduct research and analysis for rotary-wingHelicopter Division aircraft repairable items to correct asset shortfalls and maintain designated asset supply levels fabricate or procure hardware or software to be utilized in modifications/upgrades as required by individual ESTRs accomplish data mining/trend identification tasks integrate new technologies into current system architectures to enhance reliability and maintainability as specified provide engineering support to resolve electrical, avionics and EMI/EMC deficiencies on rotary-wing aircraft In the cases of EMC/EMI compatibility or where proposed mechanical or electrical solutions do not comply with form, fit, function, and interface requirements, the contractor shall analyze the test plan(s) and other existing TDPs that define the platforms to ensure possible deficiencies are detected and resolved provide hazard identification through safety analysis conducted on system/subsystem modifications, engineering change proposals, mishap data and deficiency reports provide engineering support to isolate and analyze aircraft functional system deficiencies, identify appropriate solutions and produce all engineering data required to implement the improvements to prevent an adverse impact to rotary-wing aircraft reliability and maintainability rapid response to field locations for �no notice� deficiency, grounded aircraft and mishap support assist in maintaining configuration management for rotary-wing weapon systems perform R&M evaluation and insertion of new technology into existing helicopter systems for modernization to improve performance, reliability, maintainability, and survivability of weapon systems, subsystems, and the support equipment develop and provide prototypes, pre-production items, or one-time production items in quantities as specified in the ESTR to allow for testing by both the contractor and Government. The contractor shall provide prototypes, pre-production units, or one-time production units, conduct tests and evaluate the item(s) against specified requirements, and deliver an industry-validated technical documentation package modification/changes/updates to engineering drawing packages, technical orders (TO), Flight Manuals and time compliance technical orders (TCTO) provide engineering and technical installation services to support trial install/kit proof activities as they apply to reliability and maintainability investigate failure modes for low Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) components and develop/recommend solutions to improve MTBF via component redesign, material changes and/or maintenance practice changes POCs for this RFI are: Michelle Privette, Program Manager (michelle.privette@us.af.mil) Phillip Russell, Contracting Officer (phillip.russell.9@us.af.mil) Brent Talbert, Contract Specialist (brent.talbert@us.af.mil) RFI responses are due 4 November 2026, 5:00pm EST

title: Y--AK FWS AK PEN NWR REPLACE COLD STRG 5
description: This is a Synopsis/Pre-Solicitation Notice. The final solicitation package will follow. The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (USFWS) anticipates soliciting proposals for the demolition of an existing cold storage building and the design and construction of a new detached cold storage facility at the Alaska Peninsula/Becharof National Wildlife Refuge in King Salmon, Alaska. This project is supported by the Great American Outdoor Act (GAOA) Summary: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service anticipates awarding a single firm-fixed-price design-build construction contract for the demolition of the existing cold storage building and the design and construction of a new detached cold storage facility of approximately 5,500 to 5,800 square feet. The project is located in a remote area of King Salmon, Alaska. The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, tools, supplies, transportation, shipping, handling, logistics support, and incidentals necessary to complete the work. The contractor shall be responsible for all transportation and delivery requirements associated with furnishing materials and equipment to the project site. Acquisition Information NAICS Code: 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside pursuant to FAR 19.502-2 Contract Type: Firm-Fixed-Price This acquisition will be conducted in accordance with: FAR Part 36, Construction and Architect-Engineer Contracts; and FAR Part 15, Contracting by Negotiation. In accordance with FAR 36.204(f), the estimated magnitude of construction for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. Detailed project requirements and specifications will be provided in the solicitation upon issuance. Source Selection Method The procurement will utilize: FAR Part 36.3, Two-Phase Design-Build Selection Procedures; and FAR Part 15, Best-Value Tradeoff Process. The Government intends to award one contract to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government using the tradeoff process described in FAR 15.101-1. The evaluation factors are anticipated to be: Experience and Technical Capability Past Performance Price The relative importance of the evaluation factors will be identified in the solicitation System for Award Management (SAM) Offerors must be actively registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be eligible for award. Information regarding SAM registration is available at http://www.sam.gov. Payments will be made via Electronic Funds Transfer using information contained within the contractor's SAM registration.

The tasking will be submitted via an Engineering Support Task Request (ESTR) form. data trend analysis, failure mode and effects analysis updates, preventative maintenance package task updates, AE candidate follow-up and updating existing RCM databases Targeted Analyses which would include failure analysis, follow- up analysis, and independent technical reviews The contractor shall provide engineering and technical expertise in support of avionics systems, aircraft structures, title: Post-Flood Cleanup and Disaster AbatementSand Is
description: Notice Type: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation (Commercial Item) FAR References: FAR Part 12; FAR 5.203; FAR 19.502-2 (Total Small Business Set-Aside) NAICS Code: 562910 - Remediation Services Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Product Service Code: F108 - Environmental Systems Protection - Environmental Remediation Description of Requirement The Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Canyon Country District, has an immediate abatement need for post-flood cleanup and disaster abatement at the Sand Island Ranger Station, located in a remote area approximately 4 miles west of Bluff, Utah. Flooding resulted from the San Juan River overtopping its banks and affected the following structures: * Boat House (~1,800 SF open warehouse) * Visitor Contact Center (~700 SF office/exhibition space - straw bale construction) * Law Enforcement Office (~400 SF office and sleeping area) * Residential Unit (~1,800 SF manufactured home � work primarily limited to the crawl space) The work includes hazard assessment, moisture mapping and documentation, standing water removal and drying, muck removal (excluding the residential unit), replacement of saturated flooring/baseboards and drywall where appropriate, HEPA air scrubbing, and proper disposal of debris. A detailed Statement of Work is attached. Only vendors capable of mobilizing quickly to a remote location in southeastern Utah and performing the required abatement work should compete for award. This is an urgent requirement. Work is expected to begin as soon as possible following award. Period of performance is 30 calendar days from Notice to Proceed. Site Visit A site visit is scheduled for Monday, November 2, 2026. Interested firms are strongly encouraged to attend. Vendors attending the site visit must bring all necessary personal protective equipment (PPE) appropriate for flood-damaged structures and potentially contaminated environments. Site Visit Point of Contact: Stanley Johnson Email: sjjohnson@blm.gov Phone: 435-459-2666 SAM.gov Registration All vendors must be registered and active in SAM.gov at the time of quote submission. Quotes from vendors not registered in SAM.gov will not be considered. Quote Requirements Quotes shall include the following: * Mobilization / demobilization costs (lump sum) * Equipment descriptions and quantities proposed for the work * Fixed unit rates and labor rates (by category) * Fully burdened pricing that includes all labor, materials, travel, lodging, disposal fees, and other incidental costs Evaluation Method Award will be made on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) basis. To be considered technically acceptable, an offeror must demonstrate a proven technical approach and provide evidence of prior capability to perform abatement work of this type. Among technically acceptable offers, the award will be made to the offeror with the lowest total price. Submission Instructions All quotes and offers shall be emailed to Mark Renforth at mark_renforth@ios.doi.gov. Quotes are due no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 3:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Point of Contact (Contracting) Mark Renforth Email: mark_renforth@ios.doi.gov Phone: 801-908-5005 This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued as a total small business set-aside under NAICS 562910. All responsible small business concerns may submit a quote; timely quotes will be considered. This notice does not commit the Government to award a contract.

title: Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Post-delivery support of developed?space and ground hardware and software
description: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE General Information Notice Type:?Special Notice Contracting Office:?Space RCO Title:?Notice of Intent to Sole Source - Post-delivery support of developed?space and ground hardware and software. Response Date:?No later than 1500 MST on 04 NOV 2026 NAICS Code:?541715 Product Service Code (PSC):?DA10 Description: The Space Rapid Capabilities Office (Space RCO) intends to solicit and negotiate a contract on a sole-source basis with?Systems & Technology Research, LLC, Woburn, Massachusetts?under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by RFO 6.103-1, Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. Requirement Description: Space RCO requires?post-delivery support of developed space and ground hardware and software. This effort will continue to provide systems engineering support for verification and validation of interface requirements, hardware integration and test, and on-orbit troubleshooting as the payloads are integrated onto host vehicles, tested, launched, and perform on-orbit. The instant action is to procure services to transition a prototype ground system to a full operational capability. The requirements outline a need for software development and integration expertise to enhance the existing system with a new graphical user interface (GUI), integrate mission-unique software (MUS), improve telemetry processing and data handling, and ensure the system can support long-term, 24/7 operations. The effort also requires integration with the R2C2 Acme Ground Segment, maintaining external connections, development on cloud infrastructure, and adherence to cybersecurity and systems engineering best practices. Full operational capability should be obtained within 6 months from ATP. Projected Base and Option Year CLIN Structure: CLIN 0001 (CPFF) - 2-Year Base, 3 (three) 1-Year Options. CLINs 0003, 0004 (Cost Only, No Fee) - 2-Year Base, 3 (three) 1-Year Options. CLIN 0002 (T&M) - 1-Year Base, 4 (four) 1-Year Options. Reason for Sole Source: Systems & Technology Research, LLC is the original developer of the prototype ground system. The contractor holds specialized technical expertise and existing infrastructure knowledge required to transition this system to Full Operational Capability (FOC). No other source possesses the requisite technical familiarity to meet the aggressive 6-month FOC requirement without causing unacceptable delays in fulfilling the agency's critical requirements and generating substantial duplication of costs that is not expected to be recovered through competition. Submission Details: This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. To be considered viable, any response must explicitly demonstrate the vendor's technical capability to: Achieve FOC of the specific prototype ground system within six (6) months of ATP. Perform direct, proven integration with the R2C2 Acme Ground Segment without reliance on Systems & Technology Research, LLC proprietary data. Execute the required cloud infrastructure development and 24/7 telemetry processing capabilities. (Generic marketing materials will not be evaluated.) Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract action based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses must be received no later than 1500 MST on 04 NOV 2026. Responses must be submitted via email to Monica Torrez at monica.torrez.1.ctr@spaceforce.mil and Mariacheska Legendre at mariacheska.legendre@spaceforce.mil.

title: FTC Oklahoma City- Replace Jet Bridge
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE. THIS NOTICE IS ISSUED FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION OR INVITATION FOR OFFERORS TO SUBMIT BIDS. A SYNOPSIS OF PROPOSED CONTRACT ACTION WILL BE POSTED AT A LATER DATE WHICH WILL PROVIDE INSTRUCTIONS FOR BIDDERS TO RESPOND TO THIS OPPORTUNITY. Please read all information contained herein before responding. Please do not respond to this notice if you are not seriously interested and if you do not perform this requirement as it will delay the posting of the solicitation due to further market research that will be required. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP) anticipates issuance of a solicitation for the award of a firm-fixed-price construction contract for a project titled Replace Jet Bridge at the Federal Transfer Center (FTC) in Oklahoma City, OK. FTC Oklahoma City is a federal correctional facility located at 7410 S. MacArthur Blvd., Oklahoma City, OK 73169. The work to be performed in association with this project includes the following scope: The contractor shall provide all labor, materials and equipment for the Replace Jet Bridge at FTC Oklahoma City. The project includes, but is not limited to, providing all necessary equipment, labor, materials and incidentals to remove, replace, and commissioning of one Stearns Airport Equipment Co, Inc. Jet Bridge Model # A 10, Type 61-085 Serial Number 21590A10535. The Statement of Work attachment included with the solicitation will provide complete requirements for the project but may be updated prior to issuing the solicitation. The solicitation will be posted at a later date. Access to the specifications and drawings attachments will require an active vendor registration at https://SAM.gov as well as your Marketing Partner Identification Number (MPIN) associated with your SAM registration. If you encounter problems accessing these documents, please contact the Federal Service Desk at 866-606-8220. Pursuant to Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 36.204, the estimated magnitude of the project lies between $500,000 and $1,000,000. (NOTE: This range is not meant to imply that the project has necessarily been estimated/budgeted to the maximum of the selected range. It merely conveys that the estimate/budget lies somewhere within that range). The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code applicable to this requirement is 238990 with a corresponding small business size standard of $19,000,000. Interested bidders must be registered in the SAM at www.sam.gov. The FBOP is seeking small business contractors for this project. Your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration must be less than or equal to the small business size standard specified above. Interested small business contractors are requested to respond to this notice by adding their names to the Interested Vendors List for this posting on the SAM website at https://sam.gov. You must be logged in to your vendor account in order to access the Interested Vendors List. Please add your business name only if you are interested in submitting a bid as a Prime contractor and are capable and eligible to compete for and perform this project. This notice is intended only for those who would be entering into a Prime contract with the FBOP for the entirety of the project. The FBOP does not award subcontracts. Subcontracts (if applicable/necessary) are the responsibility of the Prime contractor. The FBOP has no privity of contract with subcontractors. Interested parties are also requested to complete the attached Market Research Questionnaire and return the completed document to lwindham@bop.gov The synopsis of proposed contract action will include further instructions for responding to this opportunity. Interested bidders are advised to continuously monitor www.sam.gov for all future updates.

Yes, the response must include pricing for all five 12 month periods and shipping lines. 13What delivery location and delivery schedule apply, and are there country-of-origin or Trade Agreements requirements for the kits? The requirement says all delivery will be to MMAC in Oklahoma City, OK. 14 Please confirm that responses are due by 4:00 PM Central on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. Responses are due by 4PM 11/04/2026.

buyer: Danish Ministry of Defence Acquisition and Logistics Organisation
title: Denmark – Financial and insurance services – Udbud af delkontrakter vedrørende administration af selvforsikringsordninger
description: Forsvaret (herefter benævnt ”FMI”) er som statslig myndighed selvforsikrer, jf. cirkulære om selvforsikring i staten mv. (CIR nr. 9783 af 9. december 2005). Forsvaret har som følge heraf vedtaget interne forsikringsbetingelser, der blandt andet omfatter Forsvarets udsendte medarbejdere. Den udbudte opgave under Delkontrakt 1 omfatter administration af Forsvarets selvforsikringsordning, herunder behandling og udbetaling af refusion af skadeanmeldelser fra hele verden, der er relateret til: - Sygdom og hjemtransport - Kollektiv heltidsulykkesdækning. Opgaven omfatter også at stille en døgnbemandet alarmcentral til rådighed, der skal sikre behandling og opfølgning ved akut opståede skader og sygdom, der er omfattet af forsikringsbetingelserne. Den udbudte opgave under Delkontrakt 2 omfatter administration af Forsvarets selvforsikringsordning, herunder behandling og udbetaling af refusion af skadeanmeldelser fra hele verden, der er relateret til: - Transportskade på bohave (flyttegods ifm. udstationering, hjemkaldelse eller forflyttelse af udsendte til lokationer udenfor Danmark) - Skader i forbindelse med opmagasinering af bohave, og - Katastrofedækning. Det er den/de kommende leverandør/leverandører på delkontrakterne, der skal varetage og behandle henvendelser vedrørende skader fra den sikrede personkreds samt foretage refusion af udgifter på Forsvarets vegne. Forsikringsadministrationsordningen for hver af delkontrakterne skal udføres i henhold til de af Forsvaret opstillede betingelser, summer, dækninger og vilkår.

buyer: Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique OFCL
title: (b26055-3) Berne, Monbijoustr. 40, rénovation totale / CFC 230
description:
L'Office fédéral des constructions et de la logistique (OFCL) a commandé la rénovation totale du bâtiment situé au 40, Monbijoustrasse, à Berne. Cet édifice remarquable se compose de deux corps de bâtiment : un bâtiment de tête et une aile latérale.

Pendant la rénovation du bâtiment, les postes de travail seront transférés dans un site de relogement. Le bâtiment restera inoccupé pendant la durée des travaux. À l’avenir, il sera utilisé par l’administration fédérale et comme établissement de formation (bâtiment de tête) pour la Haute école fédérale en formation professionnelle (HEFP).

Le bâtiment administratif (ancienne Direction générale des douanes) situé au 40, Monbijoustrasse est l’un des édifices les plus emblématiques et les plus remarquables du modernisme d’après-guerre des années 1950 à Berne. Le bien est classé dans l’inventaire des bâtiments comme objet K digne de protection, fait partie d’une zone ISOS d’importance nationale (A) et figure dans l’inventaire de protection des biens culturels en tant qu’objet d’importance nationale. En conséquence, il est soumis à des exigences accrues en matière de conservation du patrimoine et sa rénovation totale est réalisée en concertation avec le service de conservation du patrimoine de la ville de Berne.

Le 3e étage de l’aile latérale doit répondre à des exigences particulièrement strictes de la conservation des monuments historiques, en raison de l’obligation de le garder dans son état historique d’origine en tant qu’étage de direction.

Au 4e trimestre 2026, des « travaux anticipés 2026 » seront réalisés.


Le présent appel d'offres porte sur la fourniture des installations à courant fort et faible, y compris le système d'éclairage de secours, les distributions secondaires, la distribution principale, les canaux de sol, la programmation KNX et les luminaires techniques. Il inclut la responsabilité globale (gestion) des livraisons et des montages effectués par les sous-traitants pour les cahiers des charges / lots suivants :

  • Lot 1 : installations électriques
  • Lot 2 : distributions électriques secondaires
  • Lot 3 : distribution électrique principale
  • Lot 4 : système d'éclairage de secours, y compris les luminaires de sécurité
  • Lot 5 : luminaires techniques et sources lumineuses

description: The overall objective of this Call is the selection of Artificial Intelligence Gigafactory (AIGF) Consortia, which will establish and operate the AIGFs and from which the Contracting Parties will acquire AI compute access time. More in detail, the specific objectives of this Call are as follows: - Selection of AIGF Consortia: Following a rigorous evaluation of the tenders by the EuroHPC JU with the support of independent experts, the Governing Board will make an award decision, establishing a ranked list of successful AIGF Consortia. - Procurement of Compute Access Time: To establish a framework for the joint acquisition of a guaranteed share of AI compute access time from the selected AIGF Consortia, formalised through the signature of a Framework Contract and a number of subsequent Specific Contracts with the successful AIGF Consortia. AIGF refers to state-of-the-art large-scale facility with sufficient capacity to handle the complete lifecycle, from development to large-scale inference, of very large AI models and applications, providing a supercomputing service infrastructure which is composed of AI-optimised computing capacity, a supporting data centre infrastructure including high-capacity storage and networking, dedicated secure cloud user access environments, and specialised secure AI-oriented support services for its advanced operations, all of which are supported by an environmentally sustainable infrastructure, in particular for energy and water supply systems.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Einführung von Ki in der Eingangsverarbeitung
description: Gegenstand des Verfahrens: Der Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio beschafft einen KI-basierten Service zur automatisierten Verarbeitung eingehender schriftlicher Sendungen (Papier/Scan, E-Mail, Fax), der als Managed Service (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) auf einer souveränen Cloud betrieben werden soll. Der KI-Service klassifiziert die Sendungen nach der Dokumentart-Systematik des Beitragsservice (DAK/SDAK), erkennt das fachliche Anliegen und extrahiert die für die Weiterverarbeitung erforderlichen Fachdaten. Die Ergebnisse werden jeweils mit einem Confidence-Score als strukturierte JSON-Objekte an den bestehenden Verarbeitungsprozess zurückgegeben. Der KI-Service wird nicht als Ersatz, sondern als Bypass zur bestehenden Eingangsverarbeitung eingeführt. Die Aussteuerung der Sendungen erfolgt über vom Beitragsservice bereitgestellte intelligente Weichen; die Kernsysteme bleiben unverändert. Nicht Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind das Scannen bzw. die Digitalisierung der Sendungen, die Ein- und Ausgangsschnittstellen der Gesamt-Eingangsverarbeitung sowie die intelligenten Weichen selbst. Der Leistungsgegenstand gliedert sich in drei Bausteine: Baustein 1 - Cloud-Infrastruktur: Bereitstellung einer souveränen, hochverfügbaren und skalierbaren Cloud-Umgebung als IaaS einschließlich bedarfsgerecht skalierbarer CPU-, GPU-, Speicher- und Netzwerkressourcen für KI-Workloads. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 2 - Managed Service: Betrieb der KI-Plattform als PaaS und SaaS, insbesondere Monitoring, Logging, Incident- und Problem-Management, Patch- und Release-Management, Backup und Recovery, Kapazitätsmanagement sowie Bereitstellung und Betrieb eines standardisierten KI-Serving-Stacks (u. a. Container-Orchestrierung, Inferenz). Der Beitragsservice behält die Hoheit über Fachlogik, Agenten sowie Auswahl und Wechsel der KI-Modelle. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 3 - Entwicklung einer individuellen Input-Management-Lösung ("KI-Service"): Konzeption, Entwicklung, Integration und Produktivsetzung einer individuellen Lösung auf Basis der bereitgestellten Plattform, einschließlich Einrichtung von Klassifikation und Extraktion je Sachverhalt, Nachweis der vereinbarten Erkennungsqualität, Schulung, Dokumentation und Unterstützung der Abnahme. Der KI-Service inkl. sämtlicher Arbeitsergebnisse (u. a. Quellcode, Konfigurationen, Prompt-Artefakte, Datenmodelle, Schnittstellenbeschreibungen, Tests, Dokumentation) geht mit zeitlich, räumlich und inhaltlich unbeschränkten Nutzungsrechten auf den Beitragsservice über. Dem Beitragsservice ist zudem das Recht einzuräumen, den KI-Service uneingeschränkt zu nutzen, zu betreiben, zu verändern und weiterzuentwickeln sowie durch Dritte betreiben oder weiterentwickeln lassen können. Es darf keine Abhängigkeit vom ursprünglichen Auftragnehmer entstehen und ein Anbieterwechsel muss grundsätzlich möglich sein. Die Lösung ist vorrangig auf Basis von Open-Source-Komponenten mit permissiven Lizenzen zu realisieren. Ergänzend ist ein Dienstleistungskontingent für weitere Sachverhalte vergleichbarer Komplexität und für Optimierungen nach der Produktivnahme bzw. Abnahme vorzusehen. Fachlicher Umfang und Mengengerüst: Schwerpunkt sind rund 1,8 Mio. formlose Schreiben pro Jahr, die bislang weder automatisch klassifiziert noch inhaltlich ausgewertet werden. Hinzu kommen rund 4,7 Mio. formgebundene Schreiben aus fünf Sachverhalten: Befreiungen, Abmeldungen, Drittschuldnererklärungen, Klärungsverfahren aufgrund Sterbefall sowie Bank- und Adressänderungen. Für die Dimensionierung ist von mindestens 6,5 Mio. Sendungen pro Jahr auszugehen (ca. 25.000 Sendungen je Arbeitstag, Spitzenwert ca. 26.700). Der Handschriftanteil liegt bei ca. 20 %. Teilweise sind besondere Kategorien personenbezogener Daten nach Art. 9 DSGVO (z. B. Gesundheitsangaben) zu verarbeiten. Wesentliche funktionale Anforderungen sind insbesondere: - KI-gestützte Texterkennung (OCR) über den gesamten Dokumentinhalt einschließlich mehrseitiger Dokumente und Anlagen; - inhaltsbasierte Klassifikation und Anliegenerkennung mittels Textverständnis statt Formularankern, einschließlich Erkennung mehrerer Anliegen je Sendung und Trennung mehrerer Dokumente; - Extraktion der Identifikationsfelder (u. a. Beitragsnummer, Name, Anschrift) und der je Sachverhalt benötigten Fachdaten, auch aus beigefügten Nachweisen; - Erkennung handschriftlicher Inhalte einschließlich freier Randnotizen, Ankreuzfelder und Prüfung auf Vorhandensein von Unterschriften; - Confidence-Scores je Ergebnis und Feld; keine Übernahme nicht belegbarer Inhalte; Schutz vor Prompt Injection; - integrierter Human-in-the-Loop-Pfad mit konfigurierbaren Aussteuerungsregeln und einer barrierefreien (BITV 2.0), deutschsprachigen, vollständig tastaturbedienbaren Nachbearbeitungsoberfläche; - Aufnahme weiterer Dokumentklassen ohne Neuaufsatz des Systems durch den Beitragsservice selbst; kein Training von Modellgewichten mit personenbezogenen Daten der Beitragszahlenden; - modellagnostische Architektur (vorzugsweise Open-Weight-Modelle), REST-Schnittstellen, Container-/Microservice-Architektur, UTF-8, Reporting (u. a. Precision/Recall/F1 je Dokumentklasse) und Anbindung an die Monitoring-Werkzeuge des Beitragsservice. Die Beschreibung der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen wird unter Ziffer 5.1. dieser Bekanntmachung fortgesetzt.

description: Auftraggeber sind die Landesrundfunkanstalten der Arbeitsgemeinschaft der öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunkanstalten der Bundesrepublik Deutschland (ARD), das Zweite Deutsche Fernsehen (ZDF) und das Deutschlandradio (DR), vertreten durch die Geschäftsführung des Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio. buyer: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
title: Germany – Foreign economic-aid-related services – 10035573-Operationalization of the circular economy in Colombia
description: Green Jobs in the Circular Economy in Colombia III (PREVEC III) is a technical cooperation project implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), in partnership with key Colombian national institutions including the National Planning Department (DNP), the Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development (MinAmbiente) and the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Tourism (MinCIT). Colombia's transition to a circular economy represents both an urgent climate imperative and a significant opportunity for sustainable economic development. PREVEC III responds to this challenge by supporting the development and scaling of climate-friendly circular economy business models in three priority sectors: textiles, tourism and agrifood, while promoting the creation of green and greened jobs and strengthening the conditions for sustainable production and consumption at national and subnational level. The project works across three interconnected areas: supporting companies to develop market-ready circular business models and access climate finance; facilitating technology transfer and innovation between German/European and Colombian partners; and translating project results into evidence-based policy dialogue at national and international level. It contributes to Colombia's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC), the national climate finance agenda and international frameworks including the Paris Agreement, the UN 10-Year Framework of Programmes on Sustainable Production and Consumption and the EU Green Deal. Results are tracked across five key dimensions: the regional scaling of circular economy business models beyond the main urban centres; small and medium-sized enterprises (SME) preparation for access to climate finance; the creation and verification of green and greened jobs with gender and vulnerability disaggregation; the application of circular economy innovations in Colombian enterprises; and corporate greenhouse gases (GHG) measurement and climate reporting. These dimensions are embedded in a results framework that links operational outputs to strategic outcomes, contributing to Colombia's climate commitments at national and international level. PREVEC III builds on a decade of GIZ engagement in circular economy in Colombia and is implemented together public institutions, private sector associations and subnational governments.

title: Germany – Engineering design services – Generalplanungsleistung für Bestandswohnimmobilien OSWO, SDWO, WEWO (Vergabenummer VOEK 394-26)
description: Die Auftraggeberin plant bundesweite Instandhaltungs- und Instandsetzungsmaßnahmen an Bestandswohnimmobilien. Gegenstand des vorliegenden Vergabeverfahren ist die Vergabe von Generalplanerleistungen an Wohnbestandsimmobilien und angemieteten Immobilien. Die von der Ausschreibung betroffenen Objekte sind insbesondere in der Auflistung der Objekte nach den jeweiligen Losen aufgeführt (siehe Anlage C-02b). Zum Leistungsgegenstand gehören auch die in den Objektlisten enthaltenen Gewerbe- und Sondergebäude. Die zu vergebenden Generalplanerleistungen umfassen insbesondere folgende Leistungen - Objektplanung Gebäude - Tragwerksplanung - Planung der Technischen Ausrüstung - Planung der Freianlagen - Planung und Beratung Bauphysik - Brandschutz einschl. Brandschutzkonzept - Koordination und Integration Gutachterleistungen - Weitere Leistungen nach Anlage C-01a und c. Je Los ist der Abschluss eines Rahmenvertrags mit zwei Rahmenvertragspartnern mit jeweils dem wirtschaftlichsten und zweitwirtschaftlichsten Bieter geplant, aus denen die Auftraggeberin sukzessiv Einzelaufträge jeweils stufenweise abrufen wird. Der Auftragnehmer hat weder einen Anspruch auf Abruf von Einzelaufträgen noch innerhalb eines vergebenen Einzelauftrags auf den Abruf aller ausgeschriebenen Leistungsphasen. Die konkreten Einzelheiten der Beauftragung ergeben sich aus der Rahmenvereinbarung und den Vereinbarungen zum Einzelauftrag. Der jeweilige Rahmenvertrag wird eine Laufzeit von 2 Jahren haben, wobei die Auftraggeberin nach Maßgabe des Vertrags durch einseitige Erklärung den Rahmenvertrag zweimal um jeweils ein Jahr verlängern kann. Die maximale Vertragslaufzeit beträgt 4 Jahre. Das jeweilige Ende der Laufzeit eines Einzelauftrags bleibt vom Ende der Rahmenvertragslaufzeit unberührt.

title: Sources Sought Installation Services of a Cable Rail Fence System
description: The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to identify companies capable of providing installation services of a cable rail fence system for the Department of Veterans Affairs, Network Contracting Office (NCO) 21, on behalf of VA Southern Nevada Health Care System. (1) The Government does not intend to award a contract based on this Sources Sought Notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited. (2) Although �proposal,� �offeror,� �contractor,� and �offeror� may be used in this source sought notice, any response will be treated as information only. It shall not be used as a proposal. (3) The purpose of this sources sought is to conduct market research to support the procurement of providing installation services of a Cable Rail Fence System for the VA Southern Nevada Health Care System at 6900 N Pecos Rd, North Las Vegas, NV 89086. This notice serves to survey the market to ascertain whether or not sources are capable of providing the requested installation services of cable rail fence system. This notice allows potential contractors/vendors to submit a non-binding statement of interest and documentation demonstrating their capability. The sources sought effort is intended to assess industry capabilities and develop/support the intended direction of acquisition planning. The Network Contracting Office (NCO 21) is requesting responses from qualified business concerns: the qualifying NAICS code for this effort is 238990 All Other Specialty Trade Contractors and Size Standard of $19M. 4) This source sought notice to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources and their size classifications (Service Disabled/Veteran Owned Small Business (SDVOSB/VOSB), Hub zone, 8(a), small, small disadvantaged, woman-owned small business, or large business) relative to NAICS 238990. Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After a review of the responses to this notice, a solicitation announcement may be published. Responses to this notice are not considered adequate responses to any corresponding solicitation announcement. All interested offerors will have to respond to the solicitation announcement in addition to responding to this notice. (5) Any information received from a contractor in response to this Sources Sought Notice may be used in creating a solicitation. Any information received that is marked with a statement, such as �proprietary� or �confidential,� intended to restrict distribution will not be distributed outside of the Government, except as required by law. Scope of Statement of Work (SOW) 1. GENERAL 1.1 Title: Installation of Government-Furnished Cable Rail Fence, Approximately 250 Linear Feet 1.2 Background: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) requires installation of a cable rail fence system at North Las Vegas Medical Center. All fence materials (posts, cable, hardware, fittings) have been procured and are on-site/in VA storage. This SOW covers labor, equipment, and incidental materials required to install the Government-furnished fence system only. 1.3 Location: The area is in front of building 5 along the parking lot sidewalk. A site walk is recommended prior to quote/proposal submission. 1.4 Period of Performance: Estimated duration: 15 work days. 1.5 Work Hours: Normal VA business hours are [0700�1630], Monday�Friday, excluding federal holidays, unless otherwise coordinated with the VA COR/Facility Engineer. Work in active patient care, parking, or pedestrian areas may require after-hours scheduling � to be confirmed at the site visit. 2. SCOPE OF WORK The Contractor shall furnish all labor, tools, equipment, consumables, and supervision necessary to install approximately 250 linear feet of cable rail fencing, Government-furnished, including: Site layout and staking of fence line per VA-approved drawing/marked layout. Excavation and setting of fence posts (line posts, corner posts, end posts, gate posts if applicable) to manufacturer specification and depth. Setting posts in concrete footings per manufacturer's installation instructions (concrete to be furnished by Contractor unless otherwise noted � confirm in RFQ). Installation of horizontal cable rail infill, including tensioning hardware, turnbuckles, and fittings per manufacturer specifications. Final tensioning, alignment, and plumb/level check of all posts and rails. Site cleanup, removal of excavation spoils, and disposal of packaging/debris (GFM packaging return to VA if required). Restoration of disturbed turf/landscaping/pavement to pre-existing condition or better. Out of Scope: Procurement of fence material, design/engineering of fence layout. electrical/grounding work. 3. GOVERNMENT-FURNISHED MATERIAL (GFM) Item Furnished By Notes Cable rail posts (line, corner, end) VA On-site / in storage on site Cable rail, fittings, turnbuckles, hardware VA Quantity to match 250 LF run Concrete for footings Contractor Unless otherwise specified Fasteners/consumables beyond kit contents Contractor Contractor is responsible for proper handling, staging, and security of GFM once received, and shall report any shortage, damage, or non-conforming material to the COR immediately upon receipt/inspection. Contractor shall return unused GFM to the VA POC upon completion. 4. APPLICABLE CODES, STANDARDS & VA REQUIREMENTS Note: Verify current edition/revision of all codes and standards against the official source prior to execution, as these are subject to periodic update. Manufacturer's published installation instructions for the specific cable rail system (governs post spacing, embedment depth, cable tension specs). OSHA 29 CFR 1926 � Excavation (Subpart P) if post holes exceed 5 ft depth or trenching is involved; general construction safety. ADA/ABA Accessibility Guidelines � if fence is adjacent to an accessible route, confirm no encroachment on required clear width. Local building code / VA Master Specification Section for site fencing, if a controlling spec exists at this facility (check with VA Facility Engineer/COR). VA Directive/Handbook requirements for construction/renovation activities on VA property, including ICRA and ILSM screening (below). 5. SAFETY & RISK CONSIDERATIONS (Flagged Items) Underground Utility Locate (Dig Permit): Mandatory call to 811/One-Call and completion of a VA Excavation/Dig Permit prior to any post hole excavation, regardless of depth. Contractor shall not break ground until utility clearance and VA permit are obtained. Excavation Safety: If any post holes exceed 5 feet in depth or trenching is required for cable runs, OSHA Subpart P (protective systems, competent person designation) applies. ICRA (Infection Control Risk Assessment): Required if work occurs near or has potential dust/vibration impact on patient care areas. Coordinate with VA Infection Control prior to mobilization. ILSM (Interim Life Safety Measures): Required if the work affects a means of egress, fire lane, or life safety system access � confirm fence location does not obstruct emergency egress routes or fire department access. PPE: Standard PPE (hard hat, safety glasses, gloves, high-visibility vest) required; steel-toe footwear if heavy posts/equipment are being handled. Cable Tensioning Hazard: Cable rail tensioning under load presents a whip/recoil hazard � Contractor shall follow manufacturer tensioning procedure and keep personnel clear of load path during final tensioning. Traffic/Pedestrian Control: If work is near parking areas, roadways, or pedestrian paths, Contractor shall provide barricades, cones, and signage per MUTCD as applicable. Concrete Work: Standard PPE for concrete handling (eye/skin protection); confirm disposal method for excess concrete/spoils. 6. SUBMITTALS Prior to start of work, Contractor shall submit for VA COR approval: Certificate of Insurance Site-specific safety plan / Job Hazard Analysis (JHA) Schedule of work / proposed sequencing Manufacturer's installation instruction

title: J041--Condenser Coils Replacement for the VA Illiana Health Care System (VAIHCS), located at 1900 E. Main Street, Danville, IL 61832.
description: Vendor Questions This amendment incorporates the Government s responses to questions submitted by potential offerors. These questions and corresponding answers are provided for clarification purposes only and do not revise or otherwise change the requirements unless explicitly stated within this amendment. Q: Please confirm how quotes are to be submitted: by email to eric.king2@va.gov, or to the Great Lakes Acquisition Center address in SF 1449 block 9 and advise any required subject line or file format. A: eric.king2@va.gov A: Return file as one document with any attachments included (PDF Preferred). A: No special subject line necessary. Q: Please provide the serial number from the CGAM060F2A nameplate, needed to order the OEM coils. A: The serial number is U10A13482 (See Picture on Last Page) Q; Is the chiller at Building 14 installed at grade or on a roof? A: The chiller is installed at grade. Q: Please confirm whether certified payroll submissions are required for the condenser-coil replacement work and identify the applicable clause and reporting instructions. A: Not Required Q: Clarification regarding refrigerant quantities, existing piping leaks, coil procurement lead times and the period of performance, and key personnel requirements. A: Period of Performance is date of award plus 30 days, per the solicitation schedule of items (B.2). This answers the coil procurement lead times. A: No Key Personnel requirements. Q: The VAAR 852.219-75 certification in the package appears with both the services limitation (50%) and the special trade construction limitation (75%, cost of materials excluded) presented. Which limitation governs this requirement? A: The correct block is Services not Special Trade Construction. So, disregard the Special Trade Construction block, as it is not applicable to this RFQ. i) [X] Services. In the case of a contract for services (except construction), the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to it to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219 73 or certified VOSBs listed in the SBA certification database as set forth in 852.219 74. Any work that a similarly situated certified SDVOSB/VOSB subcontractor further subcontracts will count towards the 50% subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded. Other direct costs may be excluded to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and small business concerns do not provide the service as set forth in 13 CFR 125.6. Q: If MK2E purchases the OEM replacement coils directly and a local subcontractor performs installation labor only, please confirm that structure is consistent with the governing limitation's calculation (materials excluded under the special trade construction prong. A: That block was incorrectly checked. See question five (5) answer. PWS 2.1 Task 4 (B)-(C) Additional Refrigerant: Q: Please confirm whether R-410A needed to replace a pre-existing shortage or loss from the existing system will be Government-furnished or separately compensated through a contract modification. A: Additional R-410A will be government furnished. PWS 2.1 Tasks 4 (A) and (B) Refrigerant Leaks Q: Existing Refrigerant Piping Leaks If additional leaks are detected outside of the condenser coils, this must be immediately brought up to the COR and CO to determine next steps Q: Coil Lead Times: A: The repair must be conducted within the time frame of the period of performance. Any issues with sourcing materials will be addressed on a case-by-case basis. PWS 9.1; Project or Site Supervisor: Q: Please confirm whether a dedicated Superintendent or Site Supervisor is required, the minimum qualifications, and whether continuous onsite presence is required whenever work is performed. Must this individual be a direct W-2 employee of the prime contractor, or may a qualified subcontractor employee serve under the prime contractor s direction and authority? Yes FAR 52.236-6, Superintendence by Contractor, mandates that at all times during contract performance from NTP through completion-the contractor must either directly superintend the work or assign a competent superintendent who * is satisfactory to the Contracting Officer (CO) * has authority to act on behalf of the contractor on-site. PWS 9.1(d); applicable safety requirements Q: Please confirm whether a designated SSHO is required and identify the minimum training, certifications, experience, and onsite attendance requirements. Must the SSHO be a direct W-2 employee of the prime contractor, or may a qualified subcontractor employee serve in this role? Yes. Contracts governed by VA specifications, a qualified employee of a subcontractor can serve as SSHO if they have formal delegation of authority from prime and their appointment is submitted and approved by the CO with adequate supporting documentation. PWS 8.3 Quality Control Manager Q: The PWS requires a Quality Control Plan. Please confirm whether a dedicated QCM is also required, and identify minimum qualifications, certifications, and onsite attendance requirements. Must the QCM be a direct W-2 employee of the prime contractor, or may a qualified subcontractor employee serve under the prime contractor s QCP? Yes, can be direct prime or subcontractor employee. Must be qualified and given formal delegation of authority. Named in quality control plan and presented to the Contracting Officer. Meet all qualifications and certifications specified. PWS 8.3 and 9.1 Combined Key Personnel Roles: Q: Please confirm whether one qualified individual may serve concurrently as Superintendent/Site Supervisor, SSHO, and QCM, or in any combination of these roles. If separate personnel are required, please identify the roles that must be separated and whether each must remain onsite whenever work is performed. Yes, they must be physically present on-site whenever work is being performed, satisfying presence requirements for all assigned roles. All other terms and conditions remain unchanged. The RFQ response date remains unchanged.

title: F138-100 engine sustainment
description: 1. Purpose This is a Sources Sought Synopsis issued for market research purposes only. This notice is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. The Government will not pay for any information, costs, or responses submitted in response to this notice. No solicitation is available at this time, and the Government does not intend to award a contract based solely on responses to this announcement. The Government may contact respondents to obtain additional information regarding their capabilities. 2. Requirement Description The Department of the Air Force is conducting market research to identify capable sources for a potential follow-on requirement for F138-100 engine sustainment supporting C-5M aircraft mission requirements. The current F138-100 Engine Sustainment contract is an indefinite delivery, indefinite-quantity service contract. The current contract was competitively awarded to Canadian Commercial Corporation. The anticipated requirement may include material management, engine maintenance, component support, engineering, airworthiness, and related sustainment services. The Government has not determined the acquisition strategy, contract type, period of performance, competition approach, or socioeconomic set-aside approach for any future requirement. 3. Anticipated Scope Interested parties should demonstrate their capability to perform some or all of the following functions: Provide material-management functions, engine maintenance, and subcontractor component-support services. Provide supply liaison support and depot-level maintenance and repair capability, including required equipment and tooling. Develop and update maintenance build plans using Reliability Centered Maintenance Plus principles. Comply with applicable Technical Order data and Time Compliance Technical Orders, including new or revised technical requirements. Support engineering investigations. Support Product Quality Deficiency Reports. Provide analytical condition inspections. Manage and use Government-furnished property, including Government-owned parts and equipment, as authorized and made available by the Government. Support and maintain certifications and compliance associated with airworthiness requirements. Integrate and coordinate peculiar support equipment. 4. Requested Capability Information Interested parties are requested to submit a concise capabilities statement addressing the following: a. Company Information Company name. Unique Entity Identifier. Commercial and Government Entity code, if available. Company address. Primary point of contact, including name, title, telephone number, and email address. Applicable NAICS codes listed in the company�s System for Award Management registration. Business size and socioeconomic status for NAICS 336412, including, as applicable: Small business; Small disadvantaged business; 8(a) participant; Women-owned small business; Economically disadvantaged women-owned small business; HUBZone small business; Service-disabled veteran-owned small business; Veteran-owned small business; or Other than small business. b. Technical Capability A description of the company�s capability to meet each anticipated scope area identified in Section 3. Identification of any scope areas the company cannot perform. Description of facilities, equipment, tooling, technical data access, quality systems, certifications, and workforce qualifications relevant to F138-100 or comparable military/commercial aircraft engine sustainment. Description of experience supporting airworthiness, technical-order compliance, engineering investigations, product quality deficiency reporting, and analytical condition inspections. c. Relevant Experience For each relevant effort performed within the past five years, provide: Customer name and contract number, if releasable; Period of performance; Brief description of work performed; Relevance to the anticipated requirement; Contract value or value range, if releasable; Prime contractor or subcontractor role; and Customer point of contact, if authorized for release. d. Teaming and Subcontracting Respondents proposing to use teaming arrangements or subcontractors should identify: Proposed prime contractor and each known teammate or subcontractor; Anticipated roles and scope allocation; Whether each entity is small or other than small business; Relevant prior teaming experience; and Any limitations, dependencies, or approvals affecting the arrangement. e. Small-Business Participation All respondents are requested to provide a reasonable estimate of anticipated small-business utilization as a percentage of total contract value, with supporting rationale. Identify the anticipated supplies or services suitable for small-business participation and the socioeconomic categories expected to be utilized. If a small business intends to compete as a prime contractor under a potential small-business set-aside, it should describe its planned approach to complying with applicable limitations on subcontracting, including: The anticipated percentage of contract performance to be performed by the prime contractor and similarly situated entities; The anticipated percentage of payments to be made to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities; The anticipated division of work among teaming partners and subcontractors; and The basis for concluding that the proposed performance approach is achievable. Other than small businesses should also describe their anticipated approach to small-business subcontracting and their experience meeting small-business subcontracting commitments on comparable efforts. 5. Acquisition Strategy The Government has not determined an acquisition strategy for this potential requirement. Information received in response to this notice will be used to assess the availability and capability of industry sources and to inform potential competition and small-business participation strategies. The Government may consider full and open competition, a socioeconomic set-aside, or another acquisition approach, as appropriate. Nothing in this notice constitutes a commitment by the Government regarding any future acquisition strategy.
